# Windows Tweak, Debloat & Optimization Tools — Complete Feature Reference

*Compiled October 2026. Covers the top 10 tools plus the honorable mentions, with what each feature actually changes (registry values, services, scheduled tasks, commands).*

## How this was built — read first

- **Open-source tools** (WinUtil, Win11Debloat, Winhance, Sophia Script, Sparkle, AtlasOS, ReviOS, RemoveWindowsAI, CrapFixer, Flyoobe, Bulk Crap Uninstaller) were cloned from GitHub and their tweak definitions were **parsed directly from the source code** (JSON configs, `.reg` files, C# setting models, PowerShell functions, YAML playbooks, INI databases). Values in those sections are what the code writes at the time of compilation; projects change quickly, so check the repo before relying on a specific value.
- **Closed-source tools** (O&O ShutUp10++, Winaero Tweaker, Autoruns, Process Lasso, NVCleanstall, DDU) were documented from official feature lists, release notes, exported configs and vendor documentation. Where a registry value is listed, it is the documented Windows/driver value the feature corresponds to, not a value traced from the tool's binary. Those sections say so explicitly.
- Very long scripts are shown truncated (`# … more lines truncated`) with the full version in the linked repo.
- Notation: `HKLM`/`HKCU` = HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE / HKEY_CURRENT_USER; `(policy)` = value lives under a `\Policies\` key (Group Policy equivalent); service startup `2` = Automatic, `3` = Manual, `4` = Disabled.

> ⚠ Many of these changes reduce security (Defender, UAC, SmartScreen, mitigations, updates) or are hard to reverse. Create a restore point / image backup before applying anything, and don't stack several all-in-one tools on the same install.

## PCOptimizer review (2026-10-10)

Every feature in this file (1929 entries) was compared with PCOptimizer (catalog of 87 tweaks, Debloat, Cleanup, Startup, Services and tasks, Apps and drivers, Tools, Health, Network and Changes pages). Features PCOptimizer already has were removed from the sections below and are listed in the appendix "Already in PCOptimizer" at the end. Every other entry carries a verdict:

| Verdict | Meaning | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| Already in PCOptimizer | Removed from the sections; see the appendix | 497 |
| Could be added (documented) | Microsoft or the vendor documents the setting; fits the catalog rules | 390 |
| Could be added only with proof | Undocumented value (often the one behind a Settings switch); allowed only with proof that it works, else Preview (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING) | 352 |
| Could be added as a tool or page feature | Not a tweak: a quick fix, a list entry, a page feature | 186 |
| Partly in PCOptimizer | The note says what exists and what is missing | 107 |
| Not suitable | Security trade-off, rejected in docs/not-included.md, undocumented and risky, obsolete on Windows 11, or out of scope | 370 |
| Needs the owner's decision | Big feature modeled on Autoruns, or a component that runs in the background | 24 |

Verdicts are an assessment, not a commitment. Before anything is added, the rules in CLAUDE.md apply: open every source before citing it, write the EN and DE explanation pages, and mark undocumented values.

### Shortlist for PCOptimizer

The candidates that came up across several tools and fit the app's rules, grouped as they could be added. Every verdict shows the entry's id (for example U0047); notes like "Same as U0047" point to that entry.

**New tweak groups (documented policies)**

- Browser privacy (Edge, Chrome, Brave): Edge policies for diagnostic data, shopping assistant, sidebar and Copilot page context, first run, default browser prompts, new tab content, Collections, Gamer Mode, desktop shortcut on update; Chrome and Brave AI and telemetry policies. Never: SmartScreen or typosquatting protection off.
- Windows AI: AllowRecallEnablement, TurnOffSavingSnapshots, DisableClickToDo, the Paint and Notepad AI policies, the generative AI and system AI model app permissions; check the newer agent policies against the WindowsAI Policy CSP first.
- App permissions: camera, microphone, notifications, motion, phone, radios, trusted devices, eye tracking and graphics capture through the documented LetApps policies, as choices that are never recommended by default.
- Windows Update without turning it off: no automatic restart while signed in, no wake for updates, deferral of feature updates, target release version, optional and preview updates, update notifications during games, Store app auto-update.
- Personalize (documented policies first): taskbar search mode, Task View button, Start lists (recently added, most used), lock screen and logon background, verbose status messages, Num Lock at sign-in, Sticky, Filter and Toggle Keys shortcuts (useful in games), long paths, AutoPlay. Values behind Settings switches (dark mode, taskbar alignment, hidden files, seconds in the clock, snap options, Dynamic Lighting, communications ducking) need proof.
- Smaller items: lock screen camera, Spotlight policies, DisablePrivacyExperience, wake timers (RTCWAKE), maintenance wake-up, PreventDeviceEncryption, BitLocker state as a check, Defender PUA and network protection as security options.

**Existing tweaks to extend**

- storage.storageSenseOn: the documented policy AllowStorageSenseGlobal could replace the undocumented per-user value and remove the Preview flag.
- privacy.suggestionsOff: DisableSoftLanding and DisableConsumerAccountStateContent policies; SilentInstalledAppsEnabled and the finish-setup and account notifications need proof.
- privacy.locationOff: the stronger DisableLocation policy as an option.
- privacy.webSearchOff: the older Windows Search policies for older builds.
- gpu.windowedOptimizations: the VRR and Auto HDR tokens in the same value.
- office.launchToThisPc: Downloads as a further choice.

**Tools and pages**

- Quick fixes: TCP/IP reset, release and renew IP, restart audio, Bluetooth, graphics driver and Windows Search, icon cache reset, time sync, performance counter rebuild, online drive check (chkdsk /scan), Windows Recovery Environment check, re-register built-in apps.
- DNS: DNS over HTTPS templates, more providers (OpenDNS, AdGuard), custom servers, reset to automatic, "use the fastest" from the benchmark.
- Apps page: uninstall desktop programs, winget upgrade, a larger reviewed catalog (game launchers, .NET Desktop Runtimes, older Visual C++).
- Debloat page: third-party promotional apps, OEM apps (with warnings for vendor update tools), discontinued apps on upgraded PCs, Edge Game Assist, and a notice when a removed app came back after a Windows update.
- Startup page: RunOnce, RunOnceEx, Active Setup and the Load value; "open location" per entry.
- Cleanup: reserved storage off for small drives; Changes page: "Open System Restore".
- Windows features: Client for NFS and a capability list.

**Decisions for the owner**

- Autoruns-style locations (codecs, boot execute, KnownDLLs, Winsock, print monitors, LSA and network providers, WMI) and startup snapshots with compare.
- Process Lasso-style rules (ProBalance, per-game power plans, priorities, CPU limits): they need a program that runs in the background all the time.

## 1. Chris Titus Tech WinUtil

**Type:** Open-source PowerShell/WPF GUI (MIT) · **Source:** github.com/ChrisTitusTech/winutil · **Launch:** `irm "https://christitus.com/win" | iex` (admin PowerShell)

**How it works internally:** Every tweak is a JSON object in `config/tweaks.json`. Registry entries are applied with `Set-ItemProperty` (`Set-WinUtilRegistry`), services via `Set-Service -StartupType` (`Set-WinUtilService`), and anything else via an embedded PowerShell `InvokeScript`. Every entry stores an `OriginalValue`/`OriginalType`/`UndoScript`, which is what the **Undo Selected Tweaks** button writes back. `<RemoveEntry>` as original value means the undo deletes the value.

**Tabs:** Install · Tweaks · Config (Features/Fixes/Legacy Panels) · Updates · Win11 Creator (MicroWin ISO builder).

### 1.1 Tweak presets

- **Standard:** Activity History - Disable; ConsumerFeatures - Disable; File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable; Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) - Disable; Location Tracking - Disable; Services - Set to Manual; Telemetry - Disable; Delivery Optimization - Disable; Disk Cleanup - Run; Temporary Files - Remove; End Task With Right Click - Enable; Restore Point - Create
  - *PCOptimizer (U0001):* Partly in PCOptimizer. Presets exist as usage profiles with "Apply recommended". Of this preset, folder type discovery is missing and WPBT was removed on purpose (docs/not-included.md); the other items exist as single tweaks.
- **Minimal:** ConsumerFeatures - Disable; Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) - Disable; Services - Set to Manual; Telemetry - Disable
  - *PCOptimizer (U0002):* Partly in PCOptimizer. Presets exist as usage profiles. WPBT was removed on purpose (docs/not-included.md); the rest exists.
- **Advanced:** Restore Point - Create; Activity History - Disable; ConsumerFeatures - Disable; File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable; Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) - Disable; Location Tracking - Disable; Services - Set to Manual; Telemetry - Disable; Delivery Optimization - Disable; Temporary Files - Remove; End Task With Right Click - Enable; Microsoft Store Recommended Search Results - Disable; Start Menu Previous Layout - Enable; Widgets - Remove; Microsoft OneDrive - Remove; Windows AI - Disable And Remove; Right-Click Menu Previous Layout - Enable
  - *PCOptimizer (U0003):* Partly in PCOptimizer. Presets exist as usage profiles. Missing from this preset: folder type discovery, Start menu previous layout (does not work on new builds), Store search results (undocumented); WPBT removed on purpose.

### 1.2 Essential Tweaks

#### Start Menu Previous Layout - Enable

*Bring back the old Start Menu layout from before the gradual rollout of the new one in 25H2. On newer versions of Windows !!THIS TWEAK WILL NOT WORK!!*  
`WPFTweaksRevertStartMenu`

| Registry path | Value | Set to | Type | Original/Undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\3036241548` | `EnabledState` | `1` | DWord | `<RemoveEntry>` |

> **PCOptimizer (U0008):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Feature override id of a staged rollout (undocumented, ViVeTool style); WinUtil itself says it does not work on newer builds.

#### Microsoft Store Recommended Search Results - Disable

*Will not display recommended Microsoft Store apps when searching for apps in the Start menu.*  
`WPFTweaksDisableStoreSearch`

Script executed:

```powershell
icacls "$Env:LocalAppData\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsStore_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\store.db" /deny *S-1-1-0:F
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
icacls "$Env:LocalAppData\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsStore_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\store.db" /grant *S-1-1-0:F
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U0009):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Edits the Microsoft Store's local database; undocumented and breaks with Store updates.

#### Services - Set to Manual

*Sets some services to Manual startup and adjusts the SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB registry value to better match system memory, which can significantly reduce the number of svchost.exe processes.*  
`WPFTweaksServices`

| Service | Set startup to | Original |
|---|---|---|
| `CscService` | Disabled | Manual |
| `DiagTrack` | Disabled | Automatic |
| `MapsBroker` | Manual | Automatic |
| `StorSvc` | Manual | Automatic |
| `SharedAccess` | Disabled | Automatic |

Script executed:

```powershell
      $Memory = (Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Measure-Object Capacity -Sum).Sum / 1KB
      Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control" -Name SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB -Value $Memory
      
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0011):** Partly in PCOptimizer. services.gamingPreset and the Services page set explained services to Manual. A long Manual list is not copied: many services already start on demand, and SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB is rejected (docs/not-included.md).

#### BitLocker - Disable

*Disables BitLocker.*  
`WPFTweaksDisableBitLocker`

Script executed:

```powershell
Disable-BitLocker -MountPoint $Env:SystemDrive
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint $Env:SystemDrive
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U0015):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Decrypts the drive: a security trade-off. Possible instead: a check that reports when BitLocker uses software encryption on an SSD, with the trade-off explained.

#### Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) - Disable

*If enabled, WPBT allows your computer vendor to execute programs at boot time, such as anti-theft software, software drivers, as well as force install software without user consent. Poses potential security risk.*  
`WPFTweaksWPBT`

| Registry path | Value | Set to | Type | Original/Undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` | `DisableWpbtExecution` | `1` | DWord | `<RemoveEntry>` |

> **PCOptimizer (U0018):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Removed in 0.4: the value is not in Microsoft's WPBT specification (docs/not-included.md).

#### File Explorer Automatic Folder Discovery - Disable

*Windows Explorer automatically tries to guess the type of the folder based on its contents, slowing down the browsing experience. WARNING! Will disable File Explorer grouping.*  
`WPFTweaksDisableExplorerAutoDiscovery`

Script executed:

```powershell
      # Previously detected folders
      $bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

      # Folder types lookup table
      $bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

      # Flush Explorer view database
      Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bags"

      Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

      # Every folder
      $allFolders = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags\AllFolders\Shell"

      if (!(Test-Path $allFolders)) {
        New-Item -Path $allFolders -Force
        Write-Host "Created $allFolders"
      }

      # Generic view
      New-ItemProperty -Path $allFolders -Name "FolderType" -Value "NotSpecified" -PropertyType String -Force
      Write-Host "Set FolderType to NotSpecified"

      Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!
      
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
      # Previously detected folders
      $bags = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags"

      # Folder types lookup table
      $bagMRU = "HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU"

      # Flush Explorer view database
      Remove-Item -Path $bags -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bags"

      Remove-Item -Path $bagMRU -Recurse -Force
      Write-Host "Removed $bagMRU"

      Write-Host Please sign out and back in, or restart your computer to apply the changes!
      
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U0022):** Could be added only with proof (undocumented value), else Preview. Could be added with FolderType = NotSpecified under Bags\AllFolders\Shell (undocumented, needs proof, else Preview). Deleting the existing Bags as WinUtil does loses saved folder views and cannot be undone.

#### Microsoft Edge - Remove

*Uninstalls Microsoft Edge by creating dummy MicrosoftEdge.exe file in the legacy Edge folder. This tricks Windows into unlocking the official Edge uninstaller allowing for a system-level removal.*  
`WPFTweaksRemoveEdge`

Script executed:

```powershell
      $Path = Resolve-Path -Path "$Env:ProgramFiles (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\*\Installer\setup.exe" | Select-Object -Last 1

      if (Test-Path $Path) {
          New-Item -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe" -Force
          Start-Process -FilePath $Path -ArgumentList "--uninstall --system-level --force-uninstall --delete-profile" -Wait
          Write-Host "Microsoft Edge was removed"
      } else {
          Write-Host "Microsoft Edge is not installed"
      }
      
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
      Write-Host "Installing Microsoft Edge..."
      winget install Microsoft.Edge --source winget
      
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U0026):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Unsupported removal trick (Edge is uninstallable only in the EEA); WebView2 and Windows parts depend on it. Edge stays protected on the Debloat page.

#### Disable Reserved Storage

*Disables Windows Reserved Storage (7-10 GB held for updates/temp files). Recommended only on small drives. Re-enable before major Windows feature updates to avoid installation failures.*  
`WPFTweaksReservedStorage`

Script executed:

```powershell
DISM /Online /Set-ReservedStorageState /State:Disabled
```

<details><summary>Undo script</summary>

```powershell
DISM /Online /Set-ReservedStorageState /State:Enabled
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U0031):** Could be added (documented). Documented DISM command (DISM /Online /Set-ReservedStorageState). Could be a Cleanup option for small system drives, with the warning to turn it back on before feature updates.

```powershell
      $Appx = (Get-AppxPackage MicrosoftWindows.Client.CoreAI).PackageFullName
      $Sid = (Get-LocalUser $Env:UserName).Sid.Value

      New-Item "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Appx\AppxAllUserStore\EndOfLife\$Sid\$Appx" -Force

      Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers "*Copilot*" | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers
      winget uninstall -e --name "Copilot" --silent --force --accept-source-agreements 2>$null
      Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.MicrosoftOfficeHub | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers

      if ($Appx) {
          Remove-AppxPackage $Appx
      }

      Set-Service -Name WSAIFabricSvc -StartupType Disabled
      Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -FeatureName Recall -Online -NoRestart

      Write-Host "Windows AI Disabled"
      
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0033):** Partly in PCOptimizer. background.aiOff (Recall snapshots policy), Copilot on the Debloat page and Recall in Windows features exist. Could be added: further documented WindowsAI policies (for example Click to Do). Removing system AI packages is not supported (N).

| Open_DNS | 208.67.222.222, 208.67.220.220 | 2620:119:35::35, 2620:119:53::53 | https://doh.opendns.com/dns-query |

### 1.6 Config tab – Windows Features

#### Network File System (NFS) - Enable

*Network File System (NFS) is a mechanism for storing files on a network.*

Enables optional features via `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -All -FeatureName`: `ServicesForNFS-ClientOnly`, `ClientForNFS-Infrastructure`, `NFS-Administration`

```powershell
nfsadmin client stop
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\ClientForNFS\CurrentVersion\Default' -Name 'AnonymousUID' -Type DWord -Value 0
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\ClientForNFS\CurrentVersion\Default' -Name 'AnonymousGID' -Type DWord -Value 0
nfsadmin client start
nfsadmin client localhost config fileaccess=755 SecFlavors=+sys -krb5 -krb5i
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0076):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Could be added to the Windows features list (Client for NFS, Pro and higher). Niche.


### 1.7 Config tab – Fixes

#### NTP Server - Enable

*Replaces the default Windows NTP server (time.windows.com) with pool.ntp.org for improved time synchronization accuracy and reliability.*

```powershell
Start-Service w32time
w32tm /config /update /manualpeerlist:"pool.ntp.org,0x8" /syncfromflags:MANUAL
Restart-Service w32time
w32tm /resync
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0081):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. w32tm is documented. A "sync time now" quick fix could be added; changing the time server is a preference, not a fix.

#### AutoLogon - Run

Downloads Sysinternals `Autologon.exe` from live.sysinternals.com and runs it with `/accepteula`. Autologon stores the password LSA-encrypted and sets `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon` → `AutoAdminLogon=1`, `DefaultUserName`, `DefaultDomainName`.

> **PCOptimizer (U0082):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Stores a password for automatic sign-in: a security trade-off, and it downloads a tool. Windows offers it itself (netplwiz).

#### Network - Reset

```powershell
netsh winsock reset
netsh int ip reset
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0084):** Partly in PCOptimizer. Tools page has DNS flush and Winsock reset. Missing: TCP/IP reset (netsh int ip reset), documented and easy to add.

### 1.10 Updates tab

#### Default (Out of Box) Settings
Deletes these values so Windows falls back to its defaults: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU` → `NoAutoUpdate, AUOptions, NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers, AUPowerManagement`; `...\WindowsUpdate` → `ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate, DeferFeatureUpdates(PeriodInDays), DeferQualityUpdates(PeriodInDays)`; `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings` → `BranchReadinessLevel, Defer*PeriodInDays`; `Device Metadata\PreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwork`; `DriverSearching\DontPromptForWindowsUpdate, DontSearchWindowsUpdate, DriverUpdateWizardWuSearchEnabled`; `DeliveryOptimization\Config\DODownloadMode`. Removes `SettingsPageVisibility=hide:windowsupdate`. Sets `BITS`/`wuauserv` → Manual, `UsoSvc` → Automatic and starts it. Re-enables all scheduled tasks under `\Microsoft\Windows\InstallService\`, `UpdateOrchestrator`, `UpdateAssistant`, `WaaSMedic`, `WindowsUpdate`, `\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\`.

> **PCOptimizer (U0103):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Resetting Windows Update policies to the defaults could be a Tools option ("remove Windows Update policies set by other tools"), similar to the leftover check (F21).

#### Disable All Updates (NOT RECOMMENDED)

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU" NoAutoUpdate 1 (DWord)
Set-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU" AUOptions 1 (DWord)
Set-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DeliveryOptimization\Config" DODownloadMode 0
foreach ($s in "BITS","wuauserv","UsoSvc") { Stop-Service $s -Force; Set-Service $s -StartupType Disabled }
Remove-Item C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\* -Recurse -Force
# Disables every scheduled task under InstallService, UpdateOrchestrator, UpdateAssistant, WaaSMedic, WindowsUpdate
```

> **PCOptimizer (U0105):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Never included: turning off Windows Update has no documented gaming benefit and leaves the PC unpatched (docs/not-included.md).

### 1.12 Win11 Creator (MicroWin) – custom ISO builder

Takes an official Windows 11 ISO and produces a debloated image:
1. Mounts the ISO (`Mount-DiskImage`), copies it to a work dir, picks an edition index (`dism /Get-WimInfo`), and mounts `install.wim` with `dism /Mount-Image`.
2. Optionally exports the **current PC's drivers** (`dism /Online /Export-Driver`) and injects them (`dism /Image:<mount> /Add-Driver /Recurse`).
3. Generates an `autounattend.xml` and injects it into the ISO. It contains a `C:\Windows\Setup\Scripts\FirstLogon.ps1` that runs on the newly installed system and: removes the AppX bloat (`Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online | Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage` / `Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers`), loads the default user hive (`reg.exe load HKU\WinUtilDefault C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT`) so tweaks also apply to future users, and writes: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\OOBE\BypassNRO=1` (local account in OOBE), `HKLM\SYSTEM\Setup\LabConfig\BypassCPUCheck/BypassRAMCheck/BypassSecureBootCheck/BypassStorageCheck/BypassTPMCheck=1` (installs on unsupported hardware), `ReserveManager\ShippedWithReserves=0`, `DeliveryOptimization\Config\DODownloadMode`, privacy values (`AdvertisingInfo\Enabled=0`, `Privacy\TailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticDataEnabled=0`, `InputPersonalization\RestrictImplicitInk/TextCollection=1`, `TrainedDataStore\HarvestContacts=0`, `Input\TIPC\Enabled=0`, `OnlineSpeechPrivacy\HasAccepted=0`, `Personalization\Settings\AcceptedPrivacyPolicy=0`), `Explorer\Advanced\TaskbarMn=0` (no Chat/Teams icon), `UnsupportedHardwareNotificationCache\SV1/SV2=0` (no 'unsupported hardware' watermark), empty Start pins via `PolicyManager\current\device\Start\ConfigureStartPins`, ContentDeliveryManager suggestion values = 0, and blocks DevHome/Outlook auto-provisioning under `WindowsUpdate\Orchestrator\UScheduler`.
4. Commits the WIM (`dism /Unmount-Image /Commit`) and builds a new bootable ISO with `oscdimg` (auto-installed via winget if missing, or from the Windows ADK). Alternatively writes directly to a USB stick (`Set-Disk -PartitionStyle GPT`, FAT32 boot partition + data partition).

> **PCOptimizer (U0142):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Builds custom Windows install media; out of scope (the app optimizes the installed Windows).

## 2. Win11Debloat (Raphire)

**Type:** Open-source PowerShell script with GUI + CLI (MIT) · **Source:** github.com/Raphire/Win11Debloat · **Launch:** `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://debloat.raphi.re/")))`

**How it works internally:** Each feature in `Config/Features.json` points to a `.reg` file in `Regfiles/`, which is imported with `reg import` (for other users / Sysprep mode it loads the target NTUSER.DAT or `C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT` with `reg load` and imports the `Regfiles/Sysprep` variants). Every `.reg` has a matching file in `Regfiles/Undo`. Before applying it can create a restore point (`Checkpoint-Computer`) and a registry backup of every value it will touch (restorable from the GUI). App removal uses `Remove-AppxPackage` / `Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage` for Store apps and `winget uninstall` for Win32 apps. Supports **Default mode** (recommended set), **Custom mode**, **App removal only**, `-Sysprep` (apply to the default user profile), `-User <name>` (apply to another user), `-RunDefaults`, `-Silent`, `-WhatIf`, config import/export.

### 2.2 Non-registry features

- **Remove HP OEM applications** (`-RemoveHPApps`): Removes HP OEM AppX packages `AD2F1837.*`: HPAIExperienceCenter, HPConnectedMusic, HPConnectedPhotopoweredbySnapfish, HPDesktopSupportUtilities, HPEasyClean, HPFileViewer, HPJumpStarts, HPPCHardwareDiagnosticsWindows, HPPowerManager, HPPrinterControl, HPPrivacySettings, HPQuickDrop, HPQuickTouch, HPRegistration, HPSupportAssistant, HPSureShieldAI, HPSystemInformation, HPWelcome, HPWorkWell, myHP.
  - *PCOptimizer (U0236):* Could be added as a tool or page feature. OEM apps (HP, Dell, Lenovo) could be added to the Debloat list after review; each needs a check that it is not a driver helper.
- **Remove all pinned apps from the start menu for this user only** (`-ClearStart`): Overwrites the user's Start menu pin file `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Microsoft.Windows.StartMenuExperienceHost_cw5n1h2txyewy\LocalState\start2.bin` with an empty template (old file backed up).
  - *PCOptimizer (U0238):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Overwrites start2.bin, an undocumented binary file; out of scope.
- **Remove all pinned apps from the start menu for all existing and new users** (`-ClearStartAllUsers`): Same as ClearStart for every existing profile and copies the empty `start2.bin` into `C:\Users\Default\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.Windows.StartMenuExperienceHost_cw5n1h2txyewy\LocalState` for new users.
  - *PCOptimizer (U0239):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Same as U0238, for all users.
- **Replace the start menu layout for this user only with the provided template file** (`-ReplaceStart`): Replaces `start2.bin` with a user-supplied template file (your own pinned layout).
  - *PCOptimizer (U0240):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Same as U0238. Microsoft's documented way is a Start layout policy (ConfigureStartPins) for managed PCs.
- **Replace the start menu layout for all existing and new users with the provided template file** (`-ReplaceStartAllUsers`): ReplaceStart for all existing users + Default profile.
  - *PCOptimizer (U0241):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Same as U0240.
- **Disable Microsoft Store app suggestions in search** (`-DisableStoreSearchSuggestions`): Edits the Microsoft Store's local search database (under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsStore_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState`) and locks it with `Set-Acl`, so Start-menu search stops showing Store app suggestions.
  - *PCOptimizer (U0242):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Edits and locks the Microsoft Store's local database; undocumented and can break Store updates.
- **Forcefully uninstall Microsoft Edge. NOT RECOMMENDED!** (`-ForceRemoveEdge`): Creates `HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdateDev` → `AllowUninstall` (empty string), creates a stub `C:\Windows\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe` (needed for the uninstaller to accept), reads `UninstallString` from `HKLM\...\Uninstall\Microsoft Edge` and runs it with `--force-uninstall` appended (`--uninstall --system-level` are already part of the string), then deletes leftover shortcuts (`Start Menu\Programs\Microsoft Edge.lnk`, Quick Launch, Desktop) and autostart entries.
  - *PCOptimizer (U0244):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Unsupported removal trick; Edge stays protected (see U0026).

## 3. O&O ShutUp10++

**Type:** Closed-source freeware (portable `OOSU10.exe`), Windows 10/11 · **Vendor:** O&O Software GmbH · **Current line:** v3.x (adds a Premium tier with background enforcement of profiles and an AI settings page; v3.3 added passkey-access settings P089/P189).

**How it works:** A GUI front end over Group Policy / registry privacy values. Each setting has an ID (`P001`, `E101`, …) and a traffic-light recommendation (green = recommended, yellow = limited, red = not recommended). Many settings exist twice: once for the **local machine** (policy under HKLM, needs admin) and once for the **current user** (HKCU) — e.g. `E1xx` = Edge machine-wide, `E2xx` = Edge current user, `C101`/`C201`, `P005`/`P006`.

**Program features:** Actions menu → *Apply only recommended settings*, *Apply recommended and somewhat recommended settings*, *Apply all settings*, *Undo all changes (factory settings)*, *Restore initial settings* (state recorded on first run), *Create a system restore point*. Import/export of `.cfg` files (`P001 +` = apply, `P001 -` = don't apply). Command line: `OOSU10.exe <file.cfg> /quiet` (silent import, used by WinUtil and many deployment scripts). Search box, group-by-category view, per-machine/per-user state, settings changed by Windows Updates are flagged so you can re-apply them.

> **Note on the registry column:** OOSU10 is closed source and O&O does not publish its exact writes. The column shows the documented Windows/Edge policy value that each setting corresponds to (the same values the setting toggles when inspected with a registry monitor). Entries left blank have no single well-documented equivalent (they combine several values, services or tasks).

### Privacy

| ID | Setting | Equivalent registry value / action | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P001` | Disable sharing of handwriting data | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\TabletPC → PreventHandwritingDataSharing = 1` | **Not suitable** (U0390): Removed in 0.4: the value exists only inside the policy "Restrict Internet communication" (docs/not-included.md). |
| `P002` | Disable sharing of handwriting error reports | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\HandwritingErrorReports → PreventHandwritingErrorReports = 1` | **Not suitable** (U0391): Same as P001: handwriting values exist only inside "Restrict Internet communication" (docs/not-included.md). |
| `P004` | Disable camera in logon screen | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Personalization → NoLockScreenCamera = 1` | **Could add (documented)** (U0393): Documented policy (NoLockScreenCamera). Fits a privacy or lock screen group. |
| `P026` | Disable advertisements via Bluetooth | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\Bluetooth → AllowAdvertising = 0` | **Not suitable** (U0397): Bluetooth AllowAdvertising exists only as an MDM policy (Policy CSP); writing the PolicyManager key directly is undocumented and can be reset by Windows. |
| `P064` | Disable suggestions in the timeline | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager → SubscribedContent-353698Enabled = 0` | **Not suitable** (U0400): Timeline does not exist on Windows 11; obsolete. |
| `P065` | Disable suggestions in Start | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager → SubscribedContent-338388Enabled = 0` | **Partly exists** (U0401): privacy.suggestionsOff turns off Start suggestions with SystemPaneSuggestionsEnabled and Start_IrisRecommendations; 338388 is the matching per-feature value (undocumented). Could be added to the same tweak with proof. |
| `P070` | Disable the possibility of suggesting to finish the setup of the device | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\UserProfileEngagement → ScoobeSystemSettingEnabled = 0` | **Could add with proof** (U0404): Value behind the Settings switch "Suggest ways to finish setting up my device" (undocumented). Could join privacy.suggestionsOff with proof. |
| `P009` | Disable biometrical features | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Biometrics → Enabled = 0` | **Not suitable** (U0406): Turns off Windows Hello biometrics: a security and convenience loss with no performance gain. |

| `P016` | Disable sending URLs from apps to Windows Store |  | **Not suitable** (U0410): No registry value or policy is known for this setting; cannot be added honestly without one. |

### Security

| ID | Setting | Equivalent registry value / action | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S001` | Disable password reveal button | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CredUI → DisablePasswordReveal = 1` | **Could add (documented)** (U0476): Documented policy (DisablePasswordReveal). Security option, not performance; low priority. |
| `S002` | Disable user steps recorder | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppCompat → DisableUAR = 1` | **Could add (documented)** (U0477): Documented policy (DisableUAR). Steps Recorder is being removed from Windows, so the value matters less every release; low priority. |
| `S008` | Disable Internet access of Windows Media Digital Rights Management (DRM) | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WMDRM → DisableOnline = 1` | **Could add (documented)** (U0479): Documented policy (WMDRM DisableOnline). Only affects the old Windows Media DRM; low value. |
| `S116` | Disable NFC (Near Field Communication) |  | **Not suitable** (U0480): No local policy is documented for turning off NFC (MDM only); radio switches belong to Settings. |
| `S117` | Disable wireless display (Miracast/WiDi) |  | **Could add (documented)** (U0481): Wireless display (projection) policies are documented (Connect: AllowProjectionToPC and related). Low value. |
| `S118` | Disable mobile broadband (cellular/WWAN) |  | **Not suitable** (U0482): No local policy is documented (MDM only); mobile broadband is turned off in Settings. |
| `S119` | Disable WiFi Direct |  | **Not suitable** (U0483): No local policy is documented (MDM only). |
| `S120` | Restrict Bluetooth pairing |  | **Not suitable** (U0484): No local policy is documented for this (MDM only). |

## 4. Winhance

**Type:** Open-source WinUI 3 / .NET app (MIT) · **Source:** github.com/memstechtips/Winhance · Installer or portable; also has a PowerShell launcher.

**How it works internally:** Every setting is a `SettingDefinition` in C# (`Winhance.Core/Features/*/Models`). A definition can contain `RegistrySettings` (with `EnabledValue`/`DisabledValue`/`RecommendedValue`, `IsGroupPolicy` = written under `\Policies\`), `PowerCfgSettings` (applied with `powercfg /setacvalueindex` + `/setdcvalueindex` on the active scheme), `ScheduledTaskSettings` (enable/disable), and `ComboBox` options that map to specific values or scripts. Winhance reads the current registry state to show each toggle's real status, has a *Recommended* button per section, config export/import (`.winhance` JSON), and it generates a `Winhance` PowerShell script + scheduled task that re-applies removals after Windows updates.

**Pages:** Software & Apps (install via WinGet / remove Windows apps, capabilities and optional features) · Optimize (Privacy, Gaming & Performance, Power, Windows Update, Notifications, Sound) · Customize (Explorer, Start Menu, Taskbar, Windows Theme) · Advanced Tools (WIM/ISO customization, autounattend.xml generator).

_333 settings parsed from source._

### 4.2 Optimize: Gaming and Performance

**Mouse Hover Time**  
`gaming-performance-mouse-hover-time` · restart required, preference

Controls how long you must hover over an element before it activates (in milliseconds). Lower values make tooltips, menus, and hover effects appear faster. Default is 400ms

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse` | `MouseHoverTime` | `` | `` | `null` | String |

- Options: 1ms (Instant) (recommended): `MouseHoverTime="1"` · 10ms (Very Fast): `MouseHoverTime="10"` · 50ms (Fast): `MouseHoverTime="50"` · 100ms (Moderate): `MouseHoverTime="100"` · 200ms: `MouseHoverTime="200"` · 400ms (Default) (default): `MouseHoverTime="400"`

> **PCOptimizer (U0763):** Could be added (documented). Hover time is documented (SystemParametersInfo SPI_SETMOUSEHOVERTIME). A preference with no measured gaming effect; Personalize group at most.

**Startup Delay for Apps**  
`gaming-performance-autostart-delay` · preference

Delay startup applications by 10 seconds after boot to improve initial system responsiveness. Windows becomes usable faster, but your startup apps take longer to load

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Serialize` | `StartupDelayInMSec` | `[10000]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |

> **PCOptimizer (U0764):** Could be added only with proof (undocumented value), else Preview. StartupDelayInMSec is undocumented; it only changes when startup apps launch. Needs proof, else Preview.

**Storage Sense**  
`gaming-storage-sense` · preference

Automatically free up disk space by removing temporary files, emptying the recycle bin, and managing downloads

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\StorageSense` (policy) | `AllowStorageSenseGlobal` | `[1, null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |
| `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\StorageSense` (policy) | `AllowStorageSenseGlobal` | `[1, null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |

> **PCOptimizer (U0766):** Partly in PCOptimizer. storage.storageSenseOn uses the per-user switch (undocumented, Preview). AllowStorageSenseGlobal is the documented policy for the same thing and could replace it, which would remove the Preview flag.

**Search Entire File System**  
`gaming-performance-explorer-search`

Search your entire file system instead of only indexed locations. This provides more complete results but is significantly slower than indexed search and increases disk activity

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Search\Preferences` | `WholeFileSystem` | `[1]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |

> **PCOptimizer (U0767):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Makes File Explorer search slower; no performance gain.

**WebView2 in Windows Search**  
`gaming-performance-search-webview2`

Allow Windows Search to use WebView2 (Edge) for rendering search results. Disabling removes Edge processes spawned by SearchHost.exe, reducing resource usage. Uses an undocumented Windows Feature Management override (feature ID 37926450) that may change in future Windows updates

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\1694661260` | `EnabledState` | `[2]` | `[1]` | `1` | DWord |
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\1694661260` | `EnabledStateOptions` | `[null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\1694661260` | `Variant` | `[null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\1694661260` | `VariantPayload` | `[null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |
| `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FeatureManagement\Overrides\8\1694661260` | `VariantPayloadKind` | `[null]` | `[0]` | `0` | DWord |

> **PCOptimizer (U0768):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Undocumented feature override id (Winhance itself says it may change); risky.

**Allow Desktop Wallpaper Compression**  
`gaming-performance-wallpaper-compression` · restarts Explorer

Allow Windows to compress wallpapers to save disk space and improve performance. Only affects images in JPEG format.

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop` | `JPEGImportQuality` | `[0, null]` | `[100]` | `100` | DWord |

Configure how Windows allocates CPU time between foreground applications and background services

**Svchost Split Threshold** — *Processor*  
`gaming-performance-svchost-split-threshold` · preference

Set the memory threshold that determines when Windows splits services into separate svchost.exe processes. Higher values group more services together, reducing process count. Select the value matching your system RAM

| Key | Value | On | Off | Recommended | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Enable VRR (G-Sync/FreeSync) optimizations for smoother gameplay. Requires a VRR-compatible monitor; this setting has no effect if your monitor does not support VRR

### 4.3 Optimize: Power

**Turn off the display** — *Display*

### 4.11 Software & Apps

**Windows Apps / Capabilities / Optional Features removal.** Selected items are removed live and also written into a generated script `BloatRemoval.ps1` (stored under `C:\ProgramData\Winhance\Scripts`) that is registered as the scheduled task **`BloatRemoval`** so the apps are removed again if a Windows update reinstalls them. Store apps: `Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers | Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers` + `Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online`; capabilities: `Remove-WindowsCapability -Online -Name`; optional features: `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName -NoRestart`. Edge and OneDrive have dedicated removal scripts (`EdgeRemovalScript.cs`, `OneDriveRemovalScript.cs`). Removed items can be reinstalled (Store apps via WinGet / msstore source).

> **PCOptimizer (U1004):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. The Debloat page removes apps for all users and keeps a list of removed apps. Winhance's idea worth taking: show when a removed app came back after a Windows update (like the drift banner for tweaks). A background task that removes apps silently is not planned.

### 4.12 Advanced Tools – WIM/ISO customization

Mounts a Windows ISO, extracts/mounts `install.wim` with `dism.exe`, can inject drivers (exported from the current PC and auto-categorized), and **embeds your current Winhance configuration into an `autounattend.xml`**: the selected registry tweaks, power settings and app removals are emitted as PowerShell sections (`ScriptPreambleSection`, `AppRemovalScriptSection`, `FeatureRegistryScriptSection`, `PowerSettingsScriptSection`, `SpecialFeatureScriptSection`) that run during Windows setup. Rebuilds a bootable ISO with `oscdimg.exe` (installed via winget if missing).

> **PCOptimizer (U1079):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Builds custom Windows install media; out of scope.

## 5. Sophia Script for Windows

**Type:** Open-source PowerShell module (MIT) by farag2 & Inestic · **Source:** github.com/farag2/Sophia-Script-for-Windows · editions for Windows 10, 10 LTSC 2019/2021, 11, 11 LTSC 2024, ARM and PowerShell 7. GUI version: **SophiApp** (separate project). This section is based on the **Windows 11** edition.

**How it works:** `Sophia.ps1` is a preset file; every line is a function call with a parameter (e.g. `DiagTrackService -Disable`). Commented lines are not executed, so you customise by (un)commenting. Each function lives in `Module/Sophia.psm1` and uses `switch ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName)` to pick what to write. Group-policy values are written to the registry and additionally recorded (private helpers `Add-Policy`/`Remove-Policy`) in an `LGPO.txt` that is imported with Microsoft's `LGPO.exe` at the end, rebuilding `Registry.pol` so the policies are visible in `gpedit.msc`. You can also call functions directly: `.\Sophia.ps1 -Functions "DiagTrackService -Disable", "UninstallUWPApps"`. `InitialActions` first checks the environment: it warns and stops if it detects third-party 'harmful tweakers' or custom Windows images (it checks for traces of e.g. Win 10 Tweaker, Ghost Toolbox, Revision Tool from ReviOS, Modern Tweaker), checks for pending reboots, Defender health and that the script files are unmodified (hash check). Tab completion: `. .\Import-TabCompletion.ps1`.

Legend: ✔ = enabled in the default preset · (blank) = commented out (available, not run by default). Code blocks show the effective registry/command lines extracted from each branch of the function.

### 5.2 Privacy & Telemetry

#### SigninInfo

- **`SigninInfo -Disable`** ✔ — Do not use sign-in info to automatically finish setting up device after an update

```powershell
New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\UserARSO\$SID"
New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\UserARSO\$SID" -Name OptOut -PropertyType DWord -Value 1
```

- **`SigninInfo -Enable`** — Use sign-in info to automatically finish setting up device after an update (default value)

```powershell
Remove-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\UserARSO\$SID" -Name OptOut
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1086):** Could be added (documented). Documented policy (DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn, automatic sign-in after an update restart). The per-user OptOut is the Settings switch. Small security gain.

## 6. Sparkle

**Type:** Open-source Electron/React desktop app (by Parcoil) · **Source:** github.com/Parcoil/Sparkle · **Site:** getsparkle.net · Install via installer, `irm https://getsparkle.net/get | iex`, winget, Scoop or Chocolatey.

**How it works internally:** Each tweak is a folder in `tweaks/<id>/` with `meta.json` (title, risk level, category, warning), `apply.ps1` and `unapply.ps1`. The Electron main process (`tweakHandler.ts`) runs the scripts through an elevated PowerShell (`powershell.ts`). Tweaks are also fetched as a bundled `registry-scripts.json` so they can be updated without a new app release. Before applying, Sparkle can create a restore point and a registry backup (Backup page).

**Pages:** Home (system info) · Tweaks · Clean · Debloat (runs the debloat-windows tweak with app selection) · Apps (winget/choco installer) · DNS · Utilities · Backup (restore points) · Settings.

### 6.1 Tweaks

#### Set 24-Hour Clock

`24-hour-clock` · risk: **safe** · category: General, Appearance

Changes clock to display 24-hour format.

> Switches Windows to a true 24-hour time format by updating the user’s regional time settings in the registry, affecting taskbar, apps, and system timestamps. IF HAVING ISSUES WITH TASKBAR, RESTART EXPLORER WITHIN SETTINGS

Apply:

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sShortTime" -Value "HH:mm"
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sTimeFormat" -Value "HH:mm:ss"
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sShortTime" -Value "h:mm tt"
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Control Panel\International" -Name "sTimeFormat" -Value "h:mm:ss tt"
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1195):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Regional time format preference; Windows Settings offers it.

#### Align Taskbar Left

`align-taskbar-left` · risk: **safe** · category: General, Appearance

Aligns the taskbar to the left side of the screen.

> Forces the Windows taskbar to align left by editing the system registry. by setting the 'TaskbarAl' registry value to 0

Apply:

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced" -Name "TaskbarAl" -Type DWord -Value 0
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced" -Name "TaskbarAl" -Type DWord -Value 1
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1196):** Could be added only with proof (undocumented value), else Preview. Same as U0065 (taskbar alignment).

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl" -Name "DisplayParameters" -Type DWord -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\CrashControl" -Name "DisableEmoticon" -Type DWord -Value 1
```

</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1198):** Could be added only with proof (undocumented value), else Preview. Same as U0045 (DisplayParameters).

#### Disable Defender RTP

`disable-defender-rtp` · risk: **risky** · category: Performance, General

Disables Defender Real-time Protection

> Sets the Defender policy DisableRealtimeMonitoring to true, instructing Windows Security to stop actively scanning files and processes in real time. For better performance

Apply:

```powershell
Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1203):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Never included: turning off Defender has no documented gaming benefit (docs/not-included.md).

#### Disable Dynamic Ticking

`disable-dynamic-ticking` · risk: **risky** · category: Performance · ⚠ May increase power consumption

Improves system responsiveness and reduces latency by disabling dynamic timer ticks.

> Disables Windows Dynamic Ticking by setting `disabledynamictick` to `yes` using `bcdedit`, which prevents the system timer from stopping to reduce input latency and improve responsiveness.

Apply:

```powershell
try {
    bcdedit /set disabledynamictick yes
    Write-Host "Dynamic Ticking disabled successfully"
  } catch {
    Write-Host "Failed to apply Dynamic Ticking tweak"
  }
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
try {
    bcdedit /set disabledynamictick no
    Write-Host "Dynamic Ticking settings restored"
  } catch {
    Write-Host "Failed to revert Dynamic Ticking tweak"
  }
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1204):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Removed in 0.4: Microsoft says the option should only be used for debugging (docs/not-included.md).

#### Disable RDP Warnings for Unsigned Files

`disable-rdp-warnings` · risk: **caution** · category: General, Privacy · ⚠  RDP files have been abused in attacks, it is strongly recommended to keep these protections enabled..

Suppresses Windows security warnings when opening unsigned Remote Desktop (.rdp) files.

Apply:

```powershell
$path = "HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\Client"
if (-not (Test-Path $path)) {
    New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null
}
Set-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "RedirectionWarningDialogVersion" -Value 1 -Type DWord
Write-Host "RDP security warnings disabled."
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
$path = "HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\Client"
if (Test-Path $path) {
    if (Get-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "RedirectionWarningDialogVersion" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Remove-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name "RedirectionWarningDialogVersion"
        Write-Host "RDP security warnings re-enabled."
    } else {
        Write-Host "Tweak was not applied."
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "Registry path does not exist, nothing to unapply."
}
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1211):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Same as U0024: the warning protects against malicious RDP files.

#### Disable Windows Recall

`disable-windows-recall` · risk: **safe** · category: Privacy, AI

Disables the Windows Recall feature for better privacy.

> This tweak sets AllowRecallEnablement to 0 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI, disabling Windows Recall at the system level.

Apply:

```powershell
New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI" -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI" -Name "AllowRecallEnablement" -Type DWord -Value 0

Start-Process "powershell.exe" -ArgumentList "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command `"Write-Host 'Disabling Windows Recall...' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host 'This may take a while depending on your internet connection. Please wait...' -ForegroundColor Yellow; try { DISM /Online /Disable-Feature /FeatureName:Recall /NoRestart; Write-Host 'Windows Recall has been disabled successfully.' -ForegroundColor Green } catch { Write-Host 'Failed to disable Windows Recall.' -ForegroundColor Red }; Write-Host 'Press any key to close...'; $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey('NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown')`"" -WindowStyle Normal
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
Remove-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI" -Recurse -Force

Start-Process "powershell.exe" -ArgumentList "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command `"Write-Host 'Re-enabling Windows Recall...' -ForegroundColor Cyan; Write-Host 'This may take a while depending on your internet connection. Please wait...' -ForegroundColor Yellow; try { DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:Recall /NoRestart; Write-Host 'Windows Recall has been re-enabled successfully.' -ForegroundColor Green } catch { Write-Host 'Failed to re-enable Windows Recall.' -ForegroundColor Red }; Write-Host 'Press any key to close...'; $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey('NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown')`"" -WindowStyle Normal
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1212):** Could be added (documented). Same as U0609 (AllowRecallEnablement).

#### Disable Taskbar Search

`disable-taskbar-seach` · risk: **safe** · category: General, Appearance

Hides the search box from the taskbar.

> Disables the search box on the Windows taskbar by setting 'SearchboxTaskbarMode' to 0 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Search. Explorer is restarted to apply the change.

Apply:

```powershell
$path = "HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Search"

if (-not (Test-Path $path)) {
```

#### Optimize Network Settings

`optimize-network-settings` · risk: **safe** · category: Network, Gaming

Changes various Windows settings to improve network latency and speeds.

> Applies a comprehensive set of netsh TCP/IP tweaks to disable latency-inducing features, enable fast open, offload networking tasks to hardware, fine-tune congestion control, and set optimal MTU, all to maximize speed, reduce CPU load, and improve responsiveness for gaming and high-performance internet use.

Apply:

```powershell
Write-Host "Applying network tweaks..."

netsh int tcp set heuristics disabled
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=internet congestionprovider=ctcp
netsh int tcp set global rss=enabled
netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=enabled
netsh int tcp set global timestamps=disabled
netsh int tcp set global fastopen=enabled
netsh int tcp set global fastopenfallback=enabled
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=custom icw=10

Write-Host "Network tweaks applied successfully."
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
Write-Host "Reverting network tweaks to defaults..."

netsh int tcp set heuristics enabled
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=internet congestionprovider=default
netsh int tcp set global rss=default
netsh int tcp set global ecncapability=default
netsh int tcp set global timestamps=default
netsh int tcp set global fastopen=default
netsh int tcp set global fastopenfallback=default
netsh int tcp set supplemental template=custom icw=4

Write-Host "Network tweaks reverted to defaults."
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1223):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Most netsh TCP global values are Windows defaults or have no measured effect on game latency (game traffic is mostly UDP); changing auto-tuning or ECN can lower throughput. Only single documented items with evidence would qualify.

#### Optimize Nvidia Settings

`optimize-nvidia-settings` · risk: **safe** · category: Performance, GPU, Gaming

Changes Nvidia Control Panel settings to improve gaming performance

> This Changes the following NVIDIA Control Panel settings:
> 
> - Image Scaling → Off
> - Ambient Occlusion → Off
> - Anisotropic Filtering → Application-controlled
> - Antialiasing – FXAA → Off
> - Antialiasing – Gamma Correction → Off
> - Antialiasing – Mode → Application-controlled
> - CUDA – GPUs → All
> - DSR Factors → Off
> - Low Latency Mode → On
> - Max Frame Rate → Off
> - Multi-Frame Sampled AA (MFAA) → Off
> - OpenGL Rendering GPU → Use NVIDIA GPU
> - Power Management Mode → Prefer Maximum Performance
> - Shader Cache Size → Unlimited
> - Texture Filtering – Anisotropic Sample Optimization → On
> - Texture Filtering – Negative LOD Bias → Allow
> - Texture Filtering – Quality → High Performance
> - Texture Filtering – Trilinear Optimization → On
> - Threaded Optimization → On
> - Triple Buffering → Off
> - Vertical Sync → Off
> - Virtual Reality pre-rendered frames → 1

Applied without a script: the main process runs the bundled `resources/nvidiaProfileInspector.exe` and imports the profile `resources/sparklenvidia.nip` into the NVIDIA driver's global (base) profile — i.e. it writes these values into the driver profile database, not the registry. Not reversible from Sparkle.

> **PCOptimizer (U1224):** Partly in PCOptimizer. The app sets low latency mode, shader cache size, texture filtering and power mode through public NVAPI. Other Control Panel settings (image scaling, ambient occlusion, anisotropic filtering, threaded optimization) would need checking against the public NVAPI headers and evidence of an effect.

#### Remove Microsoft Edge

`remove-edge` · risk: **caution** · category: Privacy · ⚠ Removing Microsoft Edge may cause issues with windows services/apps that rely on it.

Removes Microsoft Edge from Windows.

```powershell
try {
  New-Item -Path "$Env:SystemRoot\SystemApps\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge_8wekyb3d8bbwe\MicrosoftEdge.exe" -Force
  $Path = Resolve-Path -Path "$Env:ProgramFiles (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\*\Installer\setup.exe" | Select-Object -Last 1

}
catch {

}
```

#### Set PowerShell 7 as Default

`set-powershell7-default` · risk: **safe** · category: General

Sets PowerShell 7 as the default profile in Windows Terminal (installs PS7 if missing)

Apply:

```powershell
if (Test-Path -Path "$env:ProgramFiles\PowerShell\7") {
    Write-Host "PowerShell 7 is already installed."
} else {
    Write-Host "Installing PowerShell 7..."
    winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --silent
}

$targetTerminalName = "PowerShell"

if (-not (Get-Command "wt" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
    Write-Host "Windows Terminal not installed. Exiting..."
    exit
}

$settingsPath = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\settings.json"
if (-not (Test-Path -Path $settingsPath)) {
    Write-Host "Windows Terminal settings.json not found."
    exit
}

$settingsContent = Get-Content -Path $settingsPath | ConvertFrom-Json
$ps7Profile = $settingsContent.profiles.list | Where-Object { $_.name -eq $targetTerminalName }

if ($ps7Profile) {
    $settingsContent.defaultProfile = $ps7Profile.guid
    $settingsContent | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath
    Write-Host "Default profile set to PowerShell 7"
} else {
    Write-Host "No PowerShell 7 profile found."
}
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell

    Write-Host "Windows Terminal not installed. Exiting..."
    exit
}

$settingsPath = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\settings.json"
if (-not (Test-Path -Path $settingsPath)) {
    Write-Host "Windows Terminal settings.json not found."
    exit
}

$settingsContent = Get-Content -Path $settingsPath | ConvertFrom-Json

    $settingsContent.defaultProfile = $ps5Profile.guid
    $settingsContent | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 100 | Set-Content -Path $settingsPath
    Write-Host "Default profile reverted to PowerShell 5"
} else {
    Write-Host "No Windows PowerShell profile found."
}
```
</details>

#### Disable Windows Platform Binary Table

`wpbt` · risk: **caution** · category: Privacy · ⚠ Some vendor software may not run at startup.

Prevents your computer vendor from executing programs at boot, reducing potential security risks.

> Windows Platform Binary Table (WPBT) allows manufacturers to execute software each boot, including drivers or anti-theft software. Disabling WPBT improves security by blocking this mechanism.

Apply:

```powershell
# Credit to Chris Titus Tech

$regPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager"
$regName = "DisableWpbtExecution"
$applyValue = 1

if (-not (Test-Path $regPath)) {
    New-Item -Path $regPath -Force | Out-Null
}

Set-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName -Value $applyValue -Type DWord

Write-Host "WPBT execution disabled."
```

<details><summary>Unapply</summary>

```powershell
# Credit to Chris Titus Tech

$regPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager"
$regName = "DisableWpbtExecution"

if (Test-Path $regPath) {
    if (Get-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Remove-ItemProperty -Path $regPath -Name $regName
        Write-Host "WPBT execution restored to default."
    } else {
        Write-Host "Tweak was not applied."
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "Registry path does not exist, nothing to unapply."
}
```
</details>

> **PCOptimizer (U1236):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Removed in 0.4 (docs/not-included.md).

### 6.2 Utilities page

#### Graphics Driver
*Restart your graphics driver to fix display issues.*

runScript:
```powershell
$gpus = Get-PnpDevice -Class Display -Status OK -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($gpus) {
    foreach ($gpu in $gpus) {
        Write-Output "Restarting $($gpu.FriendlyName)..."
        Disable-PnpDevice -InstanceId $gpu.InstanceId -Confirm:$false
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
        Enable-PnpDevice -InstanceId $gpu.InstanceId -Confirm:$false
    }
    Write-Output "Graphics driver restart completed."
} else {
    Write-Output "No active display devices found."
}
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1241):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. A "restart graphics driver" quick fix could be added to the Tools page (Windows documents Win+Ctrl+Shift+B; pnputil /restart-device works per device).

#### Windows Search and UI
*Restart your Windows Search and UI to fix display issues. (May take a while)*

runScript:
```powershell
try {
    Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.Windows.Search | Reset-AppxPackage
    Write-Output "Microsoft.Windows.Search restart completed."
}
catch {
    Write-Output "An error occured while resetting Microsoft.Windows.Search."
}
try {
    Get-AppxPackage MicrosoftWindows.Client.CBS | Reset-AppxPackage
    Write-Output "MicrosoftWindows.Client.CBS restart completed."
}
catch {
    Write-Output "An error occured while resetting MicrosoftWindows.Client.CBS."
}
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1242):** Partly in PCOptimizer. Tools page restarts File Explorer. Restarting Windows Search (SearchHost) could be added next to it.

### 6.4 DNS page
Sets DNS on the active adapter with `Set-DnsClientServerAddress`: Cloudflare (1.1.1.1 / 1.0.0.1), Google (8.8.8.8 / 8.8.4.4), OpenDNS (208.67.222.222 / 208.67.220.220), Quad9 (9.9.9.9 / 149.112.112.112), AdGuard (94.140.14.14 / 94.140.15.15), Automatic (`-ResetServerAddresses`), Custom.

> **PCOptimizer (U1254):** Partly in PCOptimizer. DNS presets for Cloudflare, Google and Quad9 exist. Missing: OpenDNS, AdGuard, custom servers and reset to automatic.

### 6.5 Apps page / Backup page
Apps: catalog of popular programs installed through **WinGet** (`winget install <id> --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements`) or **Chocolatey** (`choco install <id> -y`, optional `--pre`; uninstall `choco uninstall <id> -y`); Chocolatey is bootstrapped with `winget install --id chocolatey.chocolatey` if missing. Backup: creates restore points (`Checkpoint-Computer -Description '<label>'`), lists them (`Get-ComputerRestorePoint`), restores (`Restore-Computer -RestorePoint <n>`) and can delete all (`vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet`).

> **PCOptimizer (U1255):** Partly in PCOptimizer. Apps page installs reviewed apps with winget; the Changes page creates restore points. Missing: a restore point list with "restore" and a manual "create restore point now". Chocolatey is out of scope.

## 7. Winaero Tweaker

**Type:** Closed-source freeware by Sergey Tkachenko (Windows 7 → 11), current version **1.65** · **Site:** winaerotweaker.com · installer or portable mode.

**How it works:** A single native app that writes registry values (HKCU or HKLM), runs `bcdedit`/`powercfg`/`net` commands, and creates scheduled tasks/shortcuts. It detects the Windows version and only shows applicable tweaks. Program features: search, bookmarks, hide unused tweaks, per-tweak *Reset to defaults*, **Reset all** (reverts every change made by the tweaker), Import/Export of all changes as an `.ini` file (since 0.8), desktop shortcut to any tweak page, sign-out/restart prompts when required.

> **About the registry column:** Winaero Tweaker is closed source. The values below are the ones Winaero's own linked articles document for each tweak (the tweaker automates those manual steps), or the standard Windows value for that setting. Feature names follow the official feature list, which dates from 2017; the Windows 11 options added in 1.20–1.65 are included where they are named in the release history.

### 7.1 Appearance

| Tweak | What it does | Registry value / command | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Aero Colors / Custom Accents** | Edit the accent colour beyond the Settings app; define up to 8 extra custom colours that appear in Settings → Personalization → Colors. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` → `AccentColor`, `ColorizationColor`; custom accents under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Accents` | **Not suitable** (U1256): Extra accent colors beyond Settings use undocumented values; cosmetic, out of scope. |
| **Aero Lite** | Activates the hidden "Aero Lite" visual style that ships with Windows. | Applies a `.theme` pointing to `%windir%\Resources\Themes\Aero\aerolite.msstyles` | **Not suitable** (U1257): Hidden visual style that Microsoft does not support; cosmetic, out of scope. |
| **Alt+Tab Appearance** | Background transparency, desktop dimming, hide open windows behind Alt+Tab; thumbnail size, spacing and margins. | `HKCU\...\Explorer\MultitaskingView\AltTabViewHost` → `Grid_backgroundPercent`, `BackgroundDimmingLayer_percent`, `Wallpaper`; classic Alt+Tab: `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer` → `AltTabSettings = 1` | **Could add with proof** (U1258): Undocumented Alt+Tab appearance values and the classic Alt+Tab switch. Personalize group, low value. |
| **Colored Title Bars** | Show accent colour on window title bars. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` → `ColorPrevalence = 1` | **Could add with proof** (U1259): Value behind the Settings switch "Show accent color on title bars". Personalize group. |
| **Dark Color Scheme** | Dark mode for apps and system. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` → `AppsUseLightTheme = 0`, `SystemUsesLightTheme = 0` | **Could add with proof** (U1260): Same as U0047 (dark mode). |
| **Inactive Title Bars Color** | Separate colour for unfocused windows. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` → `AccentColorInactive` (ABGR DWORD) | **Could add with proof** (U1261): Undocumented inactive title bar color. Personalize group, low value. |
| **Slow Down Animations** | Hold Shift to play minimise/maximise animations in slow motion. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM` → `AnimationsShiftKey = 1` | **Not suitable** (U1262): Debug animation switch; no use. |
| **Startup Sound** | Replace the boot sound with a custom .wav (restricted on newer x64 builds). | Replaces the WAVE resource 5080 in `imageres.dll(.mun)`; enable/disable via `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication\LogonUI\BootAnimation` → `DisableStartupSound` | **Not suitable** (U1263): Replaces a resource inside a system DLL; never done by this app. |
| **Theme Behavior** | Stop themes from changing mouse cursors and desktop icons. | `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes` → `ThemeChangesMousePointers = 0`, `ThemeChangesDesktopIcons = 0` | **Could add with proof** (U1264): Theme options (undocumented values behind the theme settings dialog). Low value. |

| **Icons / Menus / Message, Statusbar, System Font / Scrollbars / Window Borders / Title Bars** | Change fonts and metrics of classic Win32 UI elements (icon spacing and font, menu height, title bar height, scrollbar width, border width, system font). | `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\WindowMetrics` → `IconFont`, `IconSpacing`, `IconVerticalSpacing`, `MenuHeight`, `MenuWidth`, `MenuFont`, `MessageFont`, `StatusFont`, `CaptionFont`, `SmCaptionFont`, `CaptionHeight`, `CaptionWidth`, `ScrollWidth`, `ScrollHeight`, `BorderWidth`, `PaddedBorderWidth` (metrics stored as twips, e.g. -15 × pixels), applied with `SystemParametersInfo`. ## 8. Autoruns (Microsoft Sysinternals)

**Type:** Free, closed-source Microsoft tool by Mark Russinovich · GUI `Autoruns64.exe` + CLI `autorunsc64.exe` · part of Sysinternals Suite (`winget install Microsoft.Sysinternals.Autoruns`).

**What it is:** Not a tweaker — a complete inventory of every place Windows can auto-start code, with the ability to disable or delete each entry. Nothing is changed until you untick or delete an entry.

**How disabling works:** Registry Run-type entries are moved into an `AutorunsDisabled` subkey next to the original key (e.g. `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\AutorunsDisabled`); Startup-folder shortcuts are moved into an `AutorunsDisabled` subfolder; scheduled tasks are set to disabled; services and drivers get their start type changed to Disabled (re-ticking restores the original). **Delete** removes the entry permanently.

### 8.1 Tabs and the locations they cover

| Tab | Locations scanned | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|
| Logon | `HKLM/HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`, `RunOnce`, `RunOnceEx` (+ `Wow6432Node`), `...\Policies\Explorer\Run`, `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\Load`, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components`, Startup folders (`%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`, `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`), `HKLM\...\Winlogon\Userinit`/`Shell` additions | **Partly exists** (U1361): The Startup page lists the Run keys (64 and 32 bit), startup folders, policy Run entries and Winlogon. RunOnce, RunOnceEx, Active Setup and the Load value are missing; they could be added to the scanner. |
| Internet Explorer | Browser Helper Objects, toolbars, URL search hooks, IE extensions | **Not suitable** (U1363): Internet Explorer add-ons; IE is retired. |
| Codecs | DirectShow filters (`HKLM\Software\Classes\CLSID\{083863F1-70DE-11d0-BD40-00A0C911CE86}\Instance`), `Drivers32` audio/video codecs, Media Foundation transforms | **Owner decision** (U1367): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| Boot Execute | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` → `BootExecute`, `SetupExecute`, `Execute`, `S0InitialCommand` | **Owner decision** (U1368): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| KnownDLLs | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs` | **Owner decision** (U1371): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| Winsock Providers | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinSock2\Parameters\Protocol_Catalog9` / `NameSpace_Catalog5` (LSPs) | **Owner decision** (U1373): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| Print Monitors | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Monitors` | **Owner decision** (U1374): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| LSA Providers | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa` → `Authentication Packages`, `Notification Packages`, `Security Packages`; `SecurityProviders` | **Owner decision** (U1375): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| Network Providers | `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\NetworkProvider\Order` | **Owner decision** (U1376): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| WMI | Permanent event subscriptions in `root\subscription` (`__EventFilter` / `__EventConsumer` / binding) — a common malware persistence spot | **Owner decision** (U1377): Not in the Startup page. Adding it means a full Autoruns-style inventory; CLAUDE.md asks to check with the owner before features modeled on Autoruns. |
| Office | Office add-ins (`HKCU/HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Office\<App>\Addins`) | **Not suitable** (U1378): Office add-ins; Office is out of scope. |

### 8.2 Program features
- **Jump to Entry** (opens Regedit / Task Scheduler at the location), **Jump to Image** (Explorer), Process Explorer integration, search online.
  - *PCOptimizer (U1383):* Could be added as a tool or page feature. "Open location" (registry editor, Task Scheduler or File Explorer at the entry) could be added to Startup rows.
- **Save / Compare**: save a snapshot as `.arn` and later highlight what changed (great for "what did that installer add?").
  - *PCOptimizer (U1384):* Needs the owner's decision. Saving a startup snapshot and comparing it later ("what did that installer add?") would be useful, but it is an Autoruns feature; ask the owner first.
- **Analyze Offline System**: point at another Windows folder + user profile (e.g. a mounted disk) to inspect a non-booting system.
  - *PCOptimizer (U1385):* Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Analyzing another Windows installation offline is out of scope.
- **User** menu: view autostarts of other user accounts.
  - *PCOptimizer (U1386):* Needs the owner's decision. Startup entries of other user accounts; Autoruns feature, ask first.

### 8.3 autorunsc command line
`autorunsc64 -accepteula -a <categories> [-c|-ct|-x] [-h] [-m] [-s] [-u] [-v[rs]] [-z <systemroot> <userprofile>] [user]`
Categories: `*` all, `b` boot execute, `c` codecs, `d` AppInit DLLs, `e` Explorer add-ons, `g` sidebar gadgets, `h` image hijacks, `i` IE add-ons, `k` KnownDLLs, `l` logon, `m` WMI, `n` Winsock, `o` Office add-ins, `p` print monitors, `r` LSA providers, `s` services & drivers, `t` scheduled tasks, `w` Winlogon. `-c` CSV, `-ct` tab-separated, `-x` XML, `-h` file hashes, `-m` hide Microsoft entries, `-s` verify signatures, `-u` show unsigned/unknown only, `-v` VirusTotal lookup (`-vr` report, `-vs` submit unknown).

> **PCOptimizer (U1387):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Command line export of autostart entries; out of scope.
