## 9. Process Lasso (Bitsum)

**Type:** Closed-source, freemium (free version with nag; Pro licence) · **Vendor:** Bitsum · Components: **Process Governor** (`ProcessGovernor.exe`, the background engine that applies rules, runs as a service or at logon) + GUI (`ProcessLasso.exe`, optional). Settings live in `prolasso.ini` (per-user or global config folder).

**What it is:** A real-time process scheduler/automation layer. It does not change Windows settings globally; it continuously applies rules to running processes using documented Win32/NT APIs. Undo = remove the rule.

| Feature | What it does | Mechanism | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ProBalance** | When overall CPU load exceeds a threshold, temporarily lowers the priority (and optionally affinity / efficiency mode) of background processes that hog CPU, then restores them. Foreground and excluded processes are never touched. Configurable: system CPU % threshold, per-process CPU %, time over quota, restraint duration, exclusions. | `SetPriorityClass`, `SetProcessAffinityMask`, EcoQoS | **Owner decision** (U1388): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Performance Mode** | Forces maximum performance system-wide (no core parking, no down-clocking) while active. | Switches the active plan to *Bitsum Highest Performance* (`PowerSetActiveScheme`) | **Partly exists** (U1389): The power plan tweaks switch to Gaming or Ultimate Performance by hand; switching automatically needs a background program (see U1388). |
| **Bitsum Highest Performance plan** | Power plan installed by Process Lasso: minimum/maximum processor state 100 %, core parking disabled, other latency-oriented values. | Imported power scheme (`powercfg`) | **Not suitable** (U1390): Minimum processor state 100 % and core parking off were removed in 0.4 (docs/not-included.md). |
| **Application Power Profiles** | Switch to a chosen power plan while a specific process runs, revert when it exits. | `PowerSetActiveScheme` | **Owner decision** (U1391): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **IdleSaver** | Switch to an energy-saving plan when the PC is idle, back when you return. | Idle detection + plan switch | **Owner decision** (U1392): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Induce Performance Mode** (per process) | Performance Mode only while that process runs (e.g. a game). | as above | **Owner decision** (U1393): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Persistent priority classes** | Every time the process starts, set Idle/Below/Normal/Above/High/Realtime. | `SetPriorityClass` | **Could add with proof** (U1394): Could be set without a background program through Image File Execution Options PerfOptions (CpuPriorityClass, undocumented). High at most; realtime is never included (docs/not-included.md). Needs proof of an effect. |
| **Persistent CPU affinity** | Pin a process to chosen cores (hard affinity). | `SetProcessAffinityMask` | **Not suitable** (U1395): Fixed CPU affinity usually hurts games; for dual-CCD X3D processors the advisor recommends AMD's driver and Game Bar instead. |
| **CPU Sets** | Soft affinity – preferred cores the scheduler uses unless needed elsewhere (e.g. keep a game on P-cores / one CCD). | `SetProcessDefaultCpuSets` | **Not suitable** (U1396): Same as U1395; Windows and the AMD and Intel drivers already steer games to the right cores. |
| **I/O priority** | Very Low / Low / Normal / High disk priority per process. | `NtSetInformationProcess(ProcessIoPriority)` | **Owner decision** (U1397): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Memory (page) priority** | Lower page priority so a process's memory is trimmed first. | `NtSetInformationProcess(ProcessPagePriority)` / `SetProcessInformation(ProcessMemoryPriority)` | **Owner decision** (U1398): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Efficiency Mode** | Puts a process into Windows' EcoQoS (low power, efficiency cores). | `SetProcessInformation(ProcessPowerThrottling)` | **Not suitable** (U1399): Task Manager already offers Efficiency mode per process; a persistent rule needs a background program. |
| **Prevent Sleep** (per process) | Keeps the system and/or display awake while a process runs. | `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED / ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED)` | **Owner decision** (U1400): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Disallowed processes** | Terminate a program whenever it starts. | `TerminateProcess` on launch | **Owner decision** (U1401): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Keep running** | Relaunch a process if it exits. | watch + `CreateProcess` | **Owner decision** (U1402): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Instance count limits** | Allow only N instances of a program. | terminate extra instances | **Owner decision** (U1403): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Instance Balancer** | Spread multiple instances of the same app across cores. | affinity per instance | **Owner decision** (U1404): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **CPU Limiter** | When a process uses > X % CPU for Y seconds, reduce its available cores for Z seconds. | temporary affinity | **Owner decision** (U1405): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Watchdog (advanced rules)** | If a process exceeds a CPU/memory threshold for a period: change priority, affinity, restart, terminate, log, etc. | rule engine | **Owner decision** (U1406): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **SmartTrim** | Trims working sets of processes over a memory threshold and can purge the standby list when free RAM is low. | `EmptyWorkingSet` / `SetProcessWorkingSetSize`; `NtSetSystemInformation(SystemMemoryListInformation)` | **Not suitable** (U1407): Trimming working sets and purging the standby list makes Windows reload data from disk; Windows already manages memory under pressure. No evidence of a gain. |
| **Gaming Mode** | Shortcut that enables Performance Mode (and disables SmartTrim) when games run. | combination | **Owner decision** (U1408): Needs a program that runs in the background all the time; PCOptimizer only runs when you open it. A big new component, so ask the owner first. |
| **Responsiveness graph / Log** | Live graph of CPU load, responsiveness metric and ProBalance actions; action log. | — | **Partly exists** (U1409): The Health page shows live sensors and measures frame rate with PresentMon; a CPU responsiveness graph and an action log of automatic rules need the background program from U1388. |

Related Bitsum freeware: **ParkControl** (edit core-parking/frequency-scaling values per power plan) and **CPUBalance** (ProBalance only).

> **PCOptimizer (U1410):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. ParkControl edits core parking values; core parking changes were removed in 0.4 (docs/not-included.md).

## 10. AtlasOS & ReviOS (playbooks)

Both are **not tools that run on your Windows**, they are *playbooks*: YAML instruction sets executed by **AME Wizard** (Ameliorated) on a stock Windows install. AME Wizard runs the actions as TrustedInstaller, so it can modify protected keys, services and system files. The actions below are the literal contents of the playbooks (`!registryValue`, `!service`, `!appx`, `!scheduledTask`, `!run`, `!cmd`, `!powerShell`, `!taskKill`, `!file`). An `option:` tag means the action only runs if you ticked that option in AME Wizard; `builds:` limits it to certain Windows builds.

> ⚠ These remove/disable components system-wide (e.g. Defender optional, Windows Update behaviour, mitigations, services). Microsoft does not support the result and some changes can only be reverted by reinstalling Windows.

### 10.1 AtlasOS

**Source:** github.com/Atlas-OS/Atlas (GPL-3.0) · Supports Windows 11 (and 10 22H2). Main entry `Configuration/custom.yml` → `atlas/*.yml` + `tweaks.yml`. After install, the *Atlas folder* on the desktop holds toggle scripts (Software, Drivers, General Configuration, Interface Tweaks, Windows Settings, Advanced Configuration, Security, Additional Tools, Troubleshooting) to reverse or change many choices.

#### Core playbook files

#### Initial Configuration

`atlas/start.yml` — Performs the preliminary configuration

- PowerShell:

```powershell
function Add-ToPath ([array]$Paths) {
      $machine = [System.EnvironmentVariableTarget]::Machine
      $separator = [IO.Path]::PathSeparator

      $Paths | ForEach-Object {
            if (!(Test-Path $_ -PathType Container)) {
                  Write-Error """Path '$_' doesn't exist as a container."""
            }
      }

      $newPath = @()
      $newPath += [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', $machine) -split $separator
      if ($newPath.Count -eq 0) { Write-Warning 'The PATH variable is currently empty.' }
      $newPath += $Paths
      $newPath = $newPath | Where-Object { $_ } | Select-Object -Unique

      [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', """$($newPath -join $separator)""", $machine)
}

$modulesPath = """$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows'))\AtlasModules"""
Add-ToPath """$modulesPath""", """$modulesPath\Tools""", """$modulesPath\Scripts"""
```

- run: `DISM.exe /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:"DirectPlay" /NoRestart /All`
- run: `DISM.exe /Online /Remove-Capability /CapabilityName:"App.StepsRecorder~~~~0.0.1.0" /NoRestart`
- run: `DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup`
- PowerShell: `.\SOFTWARE.ps1`
- PowerShell: `.\SOFTWARE.ps1 -Toolbox` _(option: install-toolbox)_
- PowerShell: `.\SOFTWARE.ps1 -Brave` _(option: browser-brave)_
- PowerShell: `.\SOFTWARE.ps1 -Firefox` _(option: browser-firefox)_
- PowerShell: `.\LIBREWOLF.ps1` _(option: browser-librewolf)_
- PowerShell: `.\SOFTWARE.ps1 -Chrome` _(option: browser-chrome)_

> **PCOptimizer (U1411):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Playbook start script: enables DirectPlay, removes capabilities, cleans the component store and more in one batch. Single parts are judged elsewhere (DirectPlay: Tools page; component cleanup: Cleanup page without /ResetBase).

#### Removes the drive letter from the EFI partition.

`tweaks/misc/remove-efi-drive-letter.yml` — This happens after clean install without formatting the drive

- PowerShell:

```powershell
try {
  # Find EFI System Partition on any disk
  $efiPartition = Get-Partition | Where-Object { $_.GptType -eq '{C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B}' } | Select-Object -First 1

  if ($null -eq $efiPartition) {
    Write-Output "No EFI partition found, skipping."
    exit 0
  }

  if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($efiPartition.DriveLetter)) {
    Write-Output "EFI partition has no drive letter, skipping."
    exit 0
  }

  Write-Output "Removing drive letter '$($efiPartition.DriveLetter):' from EFI partition..."
  Remove-PartitionAccessPath -DiskNumber $efiPartition.DiskNumber -PartitionNumber $efiPartition.PartitionNumber -AccessPath "$($efiPartition.DriveLetter):\"
  Write-Output "Successfully removed EFI partition drive letter."
}
catch {
  Write-Output "Failed to remove EFI partition drive letter: $_"
  # Non-fatal error, continue installation
  exit 0
}
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1431):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Removes a drive letter from the EFI partition after a specific install problem; out of scope.

`tweaks/performance/system/disable-service-host-split.yml` — Disables Service Host splitting for much lower RAM usage and process count, excluding XBOX services to fix issues with Game Bar

- PowerShell:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services' |
  Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch 'Xbl|Xbox' } |
  Foreach-Object {
    if ($null -ne (Get-ItemProperty -Path """Registry::$_""" -EA 0).Start) {
      Set-ItemProperty -Path """Registry::$_""" -Name 'SvcHostSplitDisable' -Type DWORD -Value 1 -Force -EA 0
    }
  }
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1582):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Never included: turning off automatic updates (docs/not-included.md).

#### Disable Feature Updates

`tweaks/qol/windows-update/disable-feature-updates.yml` — Disables feature updates as they might reset tweaks, bring back bloatware and potentially break the system.

- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate` → `TargetReleaseVersion` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
- PowerShell:

```powershell
if ((Get-CimInstance -Class Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption -match 11) {$a = 'Windows 11'} else {$a = 'Windows 10'}; New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'ProductVersion' -Value $a -PropertyType String -Force
```

- PowerShell:

```powershell
$ver = (Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion').DisplayVersion; New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'TargetReleaseVersion' -Value $ver -PropertyType String -Force
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1584):** Could be added (documented). Documented Windows Update for Business policy (TargetReleaseVersion with ProductVersion): stays on a chosen feature update. Fits an update group; never as a permanent default, because releases go out of support.

#### Restrict Windows Insider

`tweaks/qol/windows-update/disable-insider.yml` — Forcefully restricts Windows Insider from being enabled to prevent extra data collection, tweaks being reverted and general instability.

- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate` → `ManagePreviewBuilds` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate` → `ManagePreviewBuildsPolicyValue` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PreviewBuilds` → `AllowBuildPreview` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PreviewBuilds` → `EnableConfigFlighting` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PreviewBuilds` → `EnableExperimentation` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsSelfHost\UI\Visibility` → `HideInsiderPage` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

> **PCOptimizer (U1585):** Could be added (documented). Documented policy (ManagePreviewBuilds). Low value.

#### Disable MSRT telemetry

`tweaks/qol/windows-update/disable-msrt-telemetry.yml` — Disables MSRT's (Malicious Software Removal Tool) telemetry features

- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\MRT` → `DontReportInfectionInformation` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\RemovalTools\MpGears` → `HeartbeatTrackingIndex` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\RemovalTools\MpGears` → `SpyNetReportingLocation` = `` (REG_MULTI_SZ)

> **PCOptimizer (U1586):** Could be added (documented). Same as U0643 (MRT DontReportInfectionInformation). The MpGears values are undocumented.

#### Disable WU Nagging

`tweaks/qol/windows-update/disable-nagging.yml` — Disables Windows Update from nagging you in any way possible, e.g. about restarting your computer.

- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU` → `NoAUAsDefaultShutdownOption` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings` → `HideMCTLink` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

> **PCOptimizer (U1587):** Could be added (documented). Documented Windows Update policies (NoAUAsDefaultShutdownOption and related). Could fit a Focus group.

#### Tweaks › scripts

#### Backup Atlas Services and Drivers

`tweaks/scripts/script-backup2.yml` — Backs up default Atlas services and drivers, after all the tweaks are finished

- PowerShell: `.\BACKUP.ps1 -FilePath """$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows'))\AtlasModules\Other\atlasServices.reg"""`

> **PCOptimizer (U1588):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Atlas infrastructure (backup of its service list); the app keeps its own backups.

#### Modify Client.CBS

`tweaks/scripts/script-clientcbs.yml` — Modifies components related to Client.CBS, the miscellaneous system package in Windows 10+

- PowerShell: `.\CLIENTCBS.ps1`

> **PCOptimizer (U1589):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Modifies the Client.CBS system package; unsupported, out of scope.

#### Disable Devices

`tweaks/scripts/script-devices.yml` — Disables devices that users would not typically need to reduce any potential system resources usage in the background

- PowerShell: `Disable-NetAdapterBinding -Name "*" -ComponentID ms_msclient, ms_server, ms_lldp, ms_lltdio, ms_rspndr`
- PowerShell: `.\DISABLEPNP.ps1`

> **PCOptimizer (U1591):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Unbinds the file sharing client, server and LLDP from all adapters; breaks network shares and discovery. Out of scope.

#### Set File Associations

`tweaks/scripts/script-file-associations.yml` — Sets file associations for the user-selected web browser and other apps

- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd` _(option: !uninstall-edge)_
- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd "Brave"` _(option: browser-brave)_
- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd "LibreWolf"` _(option: browser-librewolf)_
- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd "Firefox"` _(option: browser-firefox)_
- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd "Google Chrome"` _(option: browser-chrome)_

> **PCOptimizer (U1592):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Sets default apps through a script; Windows protects default app choices.

#### Disable Mitigations

`tweaks/scripts/script-mitigations.yml` — Disables mitigations in Windows dependent on the user's options

- cmd: `"AtlasDesktop\7. Security\Mitigations\Disable All Mitigations.cmd" /silent`

> **PCOptimizer (U1593):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Removed in 0.4: mitigations off is a security trade-off with small gains (docs/not-included.md).

#### Runs NGEN on PowerShell libraries

`tweaks/scripts/script-ngen.yml` — Optimizes PowerShell startup time by compiling the .NET libraries

- PowerShell: `.\NGEN.ps1`

> **PCOptimizer (U1594):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Precompiles PowerShell libraries; affects only PowerShell startup. Out of scope.

#### Set Profile Pictures

`tweaks/scripts/script-pfp.yml` — Sets the default Atlas profile pictures

- PowerShell: `.\PFP.ps1`

> **PCOptimizer (U1595):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Atlas branding; out of scope.

#### Configure Power Settings

`tweaks/scripts/script-power.yml` — Executes script to configure power settings for the best performance, especially focusing on the lowest latency e.g. by reducing any potential jitter

- cmd: `"AtlasDesktop\3. General Configuration\Power-saving\Disable Power-saving.cmd" /silent` _(option: disable-power-saving)_
- reg `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power` → `HiberbootEnabled` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- cmd: `"AtlasDesktop\3. General Configuration\Hibernation\Disable Hibernation (default).cmd" /silent` _(option: disable-hibernation)_
- run: `powercfg.exe /setactive "381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e"` _(option: !disable-power-saving)_

> **PCOptimizer (U1596):** Partly in PCOptimizer. power.fastStartupOff and the power tweaks overlap. Atlas' full power-saving script also sets values removed in 0.4 (core parking, minimum processor state); see docs/not-included.md.

#### Tweaks › security

#### Blocks Anonymous Enumeration of SAM Accounts

`tweaks/security/block-anonymous-enum-sam.yml` — Blocks the anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts to prevent the ability to list the potential points of attack to the system

- reg `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa` → `RestrictAnonymousSAM` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

> **PCOptimizer (U1597):** Could be added (documented). RestrictAnonymousSAM is documented (security baseline) and already the Windows default; low value.

#### Disable Remote Assistance

`tweaks/security/disable-remote-assistance.yml` — As Remote Assistance is an unused and a potential vulnerable feature, it is disabled

- reg `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance` → `fAllowFullControl` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- reg `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance` → `fAllowToGetHelp` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- run: `netsh advfirewall firewall set rule group="Remote Assistance" new enable=no`

> **PCOptimizer (U1598):** Could be added (documented). Same as U0663 (Remote Assistance).

### 10.2 ReviOS

**Source:** github.com/meetrevision/playbook · supported builds 19044/19045 (Win10) and 22631/26100/26200+ (Win11) · AME Wizard requirements: Defender toggled off, no pending updates, no third-party antivirus, internet, plugged in. Post-install management is done with **Revision Tool** (separate app).

#### Custom

`main.yml` — Custom Revision configuration

- kill process `explorer`
- kill process `SearchApp`
- kill process `SearchHost`
- kill process `RuntimeBroker`
- kill process `TextInputHost`
- kill process `ShellExperienceHost`
- kill process `backgroundTaskHost`
- kill process `Widgets`

> **PCOptimizer (U1600):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Playbook step that stops shell processes before changes; not a feature.

#### Configuration

`Tasks/final.yml` — Applies some Revision configurations

- run: `revitool.exe tweaks performance ntfs-last-access disable`
- run: `revitool.exe tweaks performance ntfs-8dot3-naming disable`
- PowerShell: `Disable-MMAgent -mc`
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Services\Pending\7971f918-a847-4430-9279-4a52d1efe18d` → `RegisterWithAU` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- cmd: `setx DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT 1`
- cmd: `setx POWERSHELL_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT 1`
- run: `PowerShell -NoP -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File CLEANER.ps1`
- reg `HKCU\System\GameConfigStore` → `GameDVR_FSEBehaviorMode` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
- PowerShell: `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath "\Microsoft\Office\*" | Disable-ScheduledTask`
- run: `revitool.exe tweaks performance service-grouping set recommended`
- run: `FINALIZE.cmd`
- run: `STARTMENU.cmd` _(option: remove-pinned-items-startmenu)_
- run: `FILEASSOC.cmd` _(option: remove-appx-photos)_
- cmd: `robocopy "Wallpapers" "%systemroot%\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\v2" /E /PURGE /IM /IT /NP`
- PowerShell: `.\WALLPAPER.ps1 -Mode Desktop -ImagePath $env:systemroot\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\v2\desktop.jpg` _(option: configure-wallpaper)_
- PowerShell: `.\WALLPAPER.ps1 -Mode LockScreen -ImagePath $env:systemroot\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\v2\lockscreen.jpg` _(option: configure-wallpaper)_
- PowerShell: `Copy-Item -Path .\WALLPAPER.ps1 -Destination "$env:systemroot\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision" -Force` _(option: configure-wallpaper)_
- PowerShell: `Copy-Item -Path .\WallpaperStartup.cmd -Destination "$env:systemroot\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision" -Force` _(option: configure-wallpaper)_
- PowerShell: `.\\Set-Theme.ps1 -Path (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot "Resources\\Themes\\dark.theme")` _(option: !configure-wallpaper)_
- PowerShell _(option: !configure-darkmode)_:

```powershell
.\Set-Theme.ps1 -New @{ WallpaperPath = (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\v2\desktop.jpg'); ThemeExportPath = (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'Resources\Themes\revi.theme'); SystemMode = 'Light'; AppMode = 'Light' }
```

- PowerShell _(option: configure-darkmode)_:

```powershell
.\Set-Theme.ps1 -New @{ WallpaperPath = (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\v2\desktop.jpg'); ThemeExportPath = (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'Resources\Themes\revi.theme'); SystemMode = 'Dark'; AppMode = 'Dark' }
```

- reg `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` → `AppsUseLightTheme` = `0` (REG_DWORD) _(option: configure-darkmode)_
- reg `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` → `SystemUsesLightTheme` = `0` (REG_DWORD) _(option: configure-darkmode)_
- reg `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` → `AppsUseLightTheme` = `1` (REG_DWORD) _(option: !configure-darkmode)_
- reg `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` → `SystemUsesLightTheme` = `1` (REG_DWORD) _(option: !configure-darkmode)_
- reg `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce` → `RevisionWallpaperStartup` = `cmd /c "%SystemRoot%\Web\Wallpaper\MeetRevision\WallpaperStartup.cmd"` (REG_SZ) _(option: configure-wallpaper)_
- remove AppX `*Client.CBS*`
- remove AppX `*StartMenuExperienceHost*` _(option: remove-pinned-items-startmenu)_
- remove AppX `*Windows.Search*`
- remove AppX `*TCUI*`
- run: `gpupdate.exe`
- run: `revitool.exe tweaks patches`
- PowerShell:

```powershell
$explorerProcess = Get-Process -Name explorer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($explorerProcess) {
  Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
}
Start-Process explorer
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1601):** Partly in PCOptimizer. Parts exist: memory.compressionOff (Preview) and storage.lastAccessOff. 8.3 names off and the GameDVR_FSE value were removed in 0.4 (docs/not-included.md); dark mode is U0047.

#### Packages

`Tasks/packages/win-sxs.yml` — Removes system (WinSxS) packages

- run: `revitool.exe winpackage --install system-components-removal`
- run: `revitool.exe tweaks security defender disable --force` _(option: disable-defender)_
- run: `revitool.exe tweaks security defender enable` _(option: enable-defender)_
- run: `revitool.exe winpackage --install ai-removal` _(option: remove-winsxs-ai)_
- run: `revitool.exe winpackage --install onedrive-removal` _(option: remove-onedrive)_

- PowerShell:

```powershell
$folderTypesKey = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\FolderTypes'
$downloadsFolderID = '{885a186e-a440-4ada-812b-db871b942259}'

$path = Join-Path -Path $folderTypesKey -ChildPath $downloadsFolderID
Get-ChildItem -Path $path -Recurse | ForEach-Object {
  if ((Get-ItemProperty -Path $_.PSPath).GroupBy) {
      Set-ItemProperty -Path $_.PSPath -Name GroupBy -Value ''
    }
}
```

- PowerShell:

```powershell
$downloadsFolderID = '{885a186e-a440-4ada-812b-db871b942259}'
$bagsPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Bags'
Get-ChildItem -Path $bagsPath | ForEach-Object {
  $fullPath = Join-Path -Path $_.PSPath -ChildPath 'Shell\{885A186E-A440-4ADA-812B-DB871B942259}'
  if (Test-Path -Path $fullPath) {
    Remove-Item -Path $fullPath -Recurse
  } 
}
```

## 11. Bulk Crap Uninstaller (BCUninstaller) — honorable mention

**Type:** Open-source (Apache 2.0) .NET app by Marcin Szeniak (Klocman) · **Source:** github.com/Klocman/Bulk-Crap-Uninstaller · v6 needs .NET 8 (portable build bundles it); installer, portable and framework-dependent builds. *(The project is currently looking for maintainers.)*

**What it does:** Finds every installed program from many sources, uninstalls many at once (quietly where possible), then scans for leftovers.

### 11.1 Detection sources (factories in `UninstallTools/Factory`)
| Source | How entries are found |
|---|---|
| Registry | `HKLM/HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall` (+ `WOW6432Node`) |
| Directory scan | Program Files / AppData folders without an uninstall entry → reported as **orphaned apps** |
| Store apps | `Get-AppxPackage` (removal: `Remove-AppxPackage -package <fullName> -confirm:$false`) |
| Windows Features | optional features via DISM |
| Windows Updates | installed updates (removal via `wusa /uninstall /kb:<n>`) |
| Steam | Steam library (removal via Steam's uninstall URI) |
| Chocolatey / Scoop | packages from those managers |
| Oculus | Oculus store apps |
| Scripts / Predefined | built-in uninstall scripts for apps that have no proper uninstaller |

> **PCOptimizer (U1652):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. An uninstaller for desktop programs (from the Uninstall registry keys, quiet uninstall through winget or the program's own uninstaller) could be added to the Apps page; Store apps are on the Debloat page.

### 11.2 Uninstaller types it understands (`UninstallerType`)
`Msiexec`, `Nsis`, `InnoSetup`, `InstallShield`, `SdbInst` (app-compat shims), `SimpleDelete` (just delete files), `PowerShell`, `StoreApp`, `WindowsFeature`, `WindowsUpdate`, `Steam`, `Chocolatey`, `Oculus`, `Unknown`. For **quiet uninstall** it uses the app's `QuietUninstallString` or generates one: MSI → `msiexec /x {ProductCode} /qn /norestart`; Inno Setup → `/VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`; NSIS → `/S`. The **UninstallerAutomatizer** helper can click through NSIS/other uninstall dialogs that have no silent mode.

> **PCOptimizer (U1653):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Same as U1652; supporting the common uninstaller types is part of that.

### 11.3 Leftover ("junk") scanners (`UninstallTools/Junk/Finders`)
Drive: `CommonDriveJunkScanner` (Program Files, AppData, ProgramData, Start Menu), `InstallLocationScanner`, `UninstallerLocationScanner`, `SpecificUninstallerKindScanner`, `PrefetchScanner`, `WerScanner` (error-report folders). Registry: `SoftwareRegKeyScanner` (`HKLM/HKCU\Software\<Vendor>\<App>`), `UninstallerKeySearcher`, `ComScanner` (CLSIDs / TypeLibs pointing to removed files), `AppCompatFlagScanner`, `AudioPolicyConfigScanner`, `DebugTracingScanner`, `TracingScanner` (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Tracing`), `EventLogScanner`, `FirewallRuleScanner`, `HeapLeakDetectionScanner`, `InstallerFoldersScanner`, `RegisteredApplicationsFinder`, `UserAssistScanner`. Misc: `ShortcutJunk` (dead shortcuts), `StartupJunk` (startup entries of removed apps). Every result gets a **confidence rating** (only "Very good" items are pre-selected); registry deletions are backed up to a `.reg` file first.

> **PCOptimizer (U1654):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Deleting leftover files and registry keys by guesswork is risky; the Storage analyzer shows large folders instead.

### 11.4 Other features
Batch uninstall with collision avoidance (runs uninstallers concurrently but never two MSI at once), optional restore point, kills processes of the app before uninstall, **Uninstall from directory** / **Target window** (drag a crosshair onto a window to find its program), certificate/signature check, startup manager, user ratings, filters (hide system components, protected, Store, updates), export list to text/HTML, command line (`BCU-console` for scripted uninstall lists).

---

> **PCOptimizer (U1655):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Batch uninstall with a restore point fits U1652. "Uninstall from window" and certificate checks are extras.

## 12. NVCleanstall (TechPowerUp) — honorable mention

**Type:** Closed-source freeware by TechPowerUp (W1zzard) · **What it is:** builds a customised NVIDIA driver installer: you pick a driver, untick components, choose tweaks, and NVCleanstall rewrites the installer package (`setup.cfg` / component manifests) and then runs NVIDIA's own `setup.exe`.

### 12.1 Workflow
1. **Driver source:** keep current version, newest available, a specific version (downloaded from NVIDIA's servers) or a local `.exe` you already have.
2. **Components:** every package in the driver is listed; untick what you don't want, e.g. NVIDIA Telemetry, NVIDIA App / GeForce Experience, ShadowPlay/Share, NVIDIA Container, HD Audio (HDMI/DP sound), PhysX, USB-C/VirtualLink driver, FrameView SDK, Shield/3D Vision legacy parts. Only the core display driver is mandatory.
3. **Tweaks page** (below), then install or just export the customised package.

> **PCOptimizer (U1656):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Builds custom NVIDIA driver packages; the app never installs drivers (it links to the vendor).

### 12.2 Installer tweaks
| Tweak | What it does | PCOptimizer |
|---|---|---|
| Disable installer telemetry & advertising | Removes the installer's own telemetry/ads calls | **Not suitable** (U1657): NVIDIA installer option; driver installation is out of scope. |
| Unattended express installation | Runs NVIDIA setup silently (`-s` style), optional **no automatic reboot** | **Not suitable** (U1658): NVIDIA installer option; driver installation is out of scope. |
| Perform a clean installation | Pre-ticks NVIDIA's "clean install" (resets driver profiles/settings) | **Not suitable** (U1659): NVIDIA installer option; driver installation is out of scope. |
| Disable driver telemetry | Prevents the telemetry module/tasks being installed | **Not suitable** (U1660): NVIDIA installer option; driver installation is out of scope. |
| Disable NVIDIA HD Audio device sleep timer | Keeps HDMI/DP audio awake (fixes cut-off audio on some VR headsets/TVs) | **Not suitable** (U1663): Driver package change; out of scope. |
| Disable HDCP | Driver class key → `RMHdcpKeyglobZero = 1` | **Not suitable** (U1664): Turns off HDCP (undocumented); breaks protected video. Out of scope. |
| Disable Ansel | Turns off NVIDIA's photo mode injection | **Not suitable** (U1665): Ansel is retired; obsolete. |
| Disable NVIDIA Container | Skips the `NvContainerLocalSystem` service (warning: breaks NVIDIA Control Panel) | **Not suitable** (U1666): Breaks the NVIDIA Control Panel (NVCleanstall warns itself). |
| Install Control Panel | Bundles the NVIDIA Control Panel instead of relying on the Microsoft Store version | **Not suitable** (U1667): Driver package choice; out of scope. |
| Show DLSS indicator | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\NVIDIA Corporation\Global\NGXCore` → `ShowDlssIndicator = 0x400` (in-game DLSS version/status overlay) | **Could add (documented)** (U1668): NVIDIA documents the DLSS indicator key in its DLSS developer material; a debug overlay, low value. |
| Remove NVENC concurrent session limit | Patches the driver with the open-source keylase `nvidia-patch` so more than the consumer limit of parallel encodes run | **Not suitable** (U1669): Patches the driver with third-party code; never done by this app. |
| Rebuild digital signature (expert) | Because a modified package is no longer NVIDIA-signed, NVCleanstall re-signs it with a locally generated certificate that it adds to the machine's trusted stores — note this security trade-off | **Not suitable** (U1670): Adds a self-made certificate to the trusted stores; a security trade-off. |
| DCH ↔ Standard handling | Recommends DCH when an old non-DCH driver (< 496.13) is installed | **Partly exists** (U1671): The advisor checks the graphics driver age (F15.gpuDriverAge) and links to the vendor; DCH or Standard handling is obsolete for current drivers. |

The MPO and NVENC tweaks were added in v1.15.0, the DLSS indicator and Container warning in v1.12.0, the HD-Audio sleep timer and "no auto reboot" option in v1.1.0, MSI mode in v1.3.0 (per TechPowerUp's release notes).

## 13. Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) — honorable mention

**Type:** Freeware by Wagnardsoft (Ghislain Harvey), portable, closed source · **What it is:** removes *every* trace of a GPU (or audio) driver when the normal uninstaller leaves remnants — used before switching GPU vendor or when a driver is corrupted.

### 13.1 Main options
| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Device type | **GPU** (NVIDIA / AMD / Intel) or **Audio** (Realtek, Sound Blaster, …) + vendor |
| **Clean and restart** (recommended) | Removes the driver, reboots so Windows comes up with the basic display driver |
| Clean and do NOT restart | For removing several drivers in a row (may leave the system unstable until reboot) |
| Clean and shutdown | For physically swapping the graphics card |
| Safe Mode launch | DDU recommends Safe Mode; it can reboot into it for you (`bcdedit /set {current} safeboot minimal` + auto-start of DDU, flag removed afterwards) |
| Prevent driver downloads from Windows Update | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DriverSearching` → `SearchOrderConfig = 0` (stops Windows reinstalling its own GPU driver after the reboot); can be reverted from the options |
| Create a system restore point | before cleaning |
| Remove vendor extras (options) | NVIDIA: PhysX, GeForce Experience / NVIDIA App, `C:\NVIDIA` folder, NVIDIA Broadcast; AMD: `C:\AMD` installer folder, AMD audio bus, Adrenalin settings; Intel: Arc Control/Graphics Command Center; Vulkan runtime entries; monitor devices (re-detected after reboot) |
| Logging | Writes a detailed log of everything removed |

> **PCOptimizer (U1673):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. The app does not remove drivers. Advice could be added: when switching GPU vendor or after driver problems, a clean removal (DDU in safe mode) helps; a link to the tool's official page.

### 13.2 What a clean actually removes
Uninstalls the device(s) through SetupAPI, deletes the vendor's `oem*.inf` packages from the Driver Store (equivalent to `pnputil /delete-driver oemNN.inf /uninstall /force`) including `System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\<pkg>` folders, deletes driver/service entries under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services`, display class subkeys under `Control\Class\{4d36e968-e325-11ce-bfc1-08002be10318}`, Windows Installer product registrations, uninstall entries, COM registrations, vendor folders in Program Files / ProgramData / AppData, vendor scheduled tasks, shortcuts and shell extensions.

> **PCOptimizer (U1674):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Driver removal from the driver store; out of scope (see U1673 for advice).

### 13.3 Command line
DDU can run unattended with switches such as `-silent`, `-clean<vendor>` (e.g. `-cleannvidia`, `-cleanamd`, `-cleanintel`), `-restart` / `-shutdown` / `-noreboot`, `-logging` and options for PhysX/GFE removal. See the readme shipped with DDU for the exact switch list of your version.

---

> **PCOptimizer (U1675):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Command line of a third-party tool; out of scope.

## 14. RemoveWindowsAI (zoicware) — honorable mention

**Type:** Open-source PowerShell script with WPF UI · **Source:** github.com/zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI · Must run in Windows PowerShell 5.1 as admin. Launch: `& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zoicware/RemoveWindowsAI/main/RemoveWindowsAi.ps1")))` · CLI: `-nonInteractive` with `-AllOptions` or `-Options DisableRegKeys,PreventAIPackageReinstall,DisableCopilotPolicies,RemoveAppxPackages,RemoveRecallFeature,RemoveCBSPackages,RemoveAIFiles,HideAIComponents,DisableRewrite,RemoveWindowsAITasks,UpdateCleanupCheck,DisableDefenderAI` (`-ExcludeOptions` inverts), `-InstallClassicApps photoviewer,mspaint,snippingtool,notepad,photoslegacy`, `-revertMode`, `-backupMode`, `-RunWinUpdateRepair`, `-EnableLogging`.

**How it works:** Uses `Reg.exe` for most writes; protected keys and files are modified by running commands as **TrustedInstaller/SYSTEM** (helper `Run-Trusted` creates a temporary scheduled task). Machine policies are also written into the local `Registry.pol` (`Edit-PolFile`) so they survive and appear in gpedit. Backup/revert mode records original values. A restore point is created first.

### Disable Registry Keys

`Disable-Registry-Keys` — Writes registry/policy values that switch off Copilot, Recall, Input Insights, Edge Copilot, Paint AI, AI Fabric service, AI Actions, Voice Access, AI voice effects, AI in Settings search, Gaming Copilot, Office Copilot, Photos AI, Click to Do. Feature IDs are disabled with an embedded `Set-FeatureID` helper (ViVeTool-style obfuscated feature IDs).

**Core AI policies** (written with `Reg.exe` *and* into `Registry.pol` via `Edit-PolFile`): `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI` → `DisableAIDataAnalysis = 1`, `AllowRecallEnablement = 0`, `DisableClickToDo = 1`, `TurnOffSavingSnapshots = 1`, `DisableSettingsAgent = 1`, `DisableAgentConnectors = 1`, `DisableAgentWorkspaces = 1`, `DisableRemoteAgentConnectors = 1`; `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI` → `DisableAIDataAnalysis = 1`, `DisableClickToDo = 1`; `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsCopilot` → `TurnOffWindowsCopilot = 1`. Revert mode writes the opposite values. Also removes Copilot auto-launch entries (`HKCU\...\RunNotification`), blocks AI shell extensions via `Shell Extensions\Blocked`, and blocks AI device instances through `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyInstanceIDs`.

| Op | Key | Value | Type | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Prevent reinstall of AI packages

`Install-NOAIPackage` — Builds and installs a custom CBS (servicing) package that marks the AI packages as removed so Windows Update does not reinstall them.

```powershell
Remove-WindowsPackage -Online -PackageName $package.PackageName -NoRestart
dism.exe /Online /remove-package /PackageName:$($package.PackageName) /NoRestart
Remove-Item -Path $value.PSPath -Recurse -Force
dism.exe /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:"$PSScriptRoot\RemoveWindowsAIPackage\$arch\ZoicwareRemoveWindowsAI-$($arch)1.0.0.1.cab" /NoRestart /IgnoreCheck >$null
dism.exe /Online /Add-Package /PackagePath:"$($tempDir)ZoicwareRemoveWindowsAI-$($arch)1.0.0.1.cab" /NoRestart /IgnoreCheck >$null
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1677):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Installs a custom servicing package to block reinstalls; unsupported.

### Disable Copilot policies

`Disable-Copilot-Policies` — Edits `C:\Windows\System32\IntegratedServicesRegionPolicySet.json` (region-based feature policy file) so Copilot/Recall policies are set to disabled for every region; takes ownership of the file first.

```powershell
takeown /f $JSONPath
icacls $JSONPath /grant *S-1-5-32-544:F /t
Set-Content $JSONPath -Value $newJSONContent -Force
takeown /f $visualAssistPath
icacls $visualAssistPath /grant *S-1-5-32-544:F /t
Set-Content $visualAssistPath -Value $newJSONContent -Force
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1678):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Edits a protected system policy file after taking ownership; unsupported.

### Remove AI packages from CBS

`Remove-AI-CBS-Packages` — Unhides hidden/locked AI packages in the component store (sets `Visibility = 1` and removes `Owners` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\Packages\<pkg>`), then removes them with DISM.

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty "registry::$($_.Name)" -Name Visibility -Value 1 -Force
New-ItemProperty "registry::$($_.Name)" -Name DefVis -PropertyType DWord -Value 2 -Force
Remove-Item "registry::$($_.Name)\Owners" -Force
Remove-Item "registry::$($_.Name)\Updates" -Force
Remove-WindowsPackage -Online -PackageName $_.PSChildName -NoRestart
Remove-Item $path.FullName -Force
dism.exe /Online /Remove-Package /PackageName:$($_.PSChildName) /NoRestart /Quiet
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1681):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Unhides and removes locked component store packages; unsupported.

`Remove-WindowsAI-Tasks`

```powershell
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '*WindowsAI*' | Disable-ScheduledTask

Remove-Item "`$env:Systemroot\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\Office\Office Actions Server" -Force
Remove-Item "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\`$officeConfigID" -Recurse -Force
```

### Update cleanup check

`Update-Cleanup-Check` — Registers a scheduled task running `RemoveAI-UpdateCleanup.ps1` that detects a new Windows build and re-removes newly installed AI components.

```powershell
Set-Content -Path $scriptPath -Value $scriptContent.Content -Force
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '\' -TaskName 'RemoveAI-UpdateCleanupChecker' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Principal $principal -Settings $settings -Force
Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'RemoveAI-UpdateCleanupChecker' -Confirm:$false
Remove-Item "$env:ProgramData\RemoveAI-UpdateCleanup-Silent.vbs" -Force
Remove-Item "$env:ProgramData\RemoveAI-UpdateCleanup.ps1" -Force
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1686):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Background task that removes components again after updates; see U1004 for the planned "came back" notice instead.

### Install classic apps

`install-classicapps` — Options: classic Notepad, classic Paint, classic Snipping Tool, Windows Photo Viewer (re-registers file associations), Photos Legacy (from the Store).

```powershell
Copy-Item -Path $sourceDir -Destination $destDir -Recurse -Force
Remove-Item "$($tempDir)RemoveWindowsAI-main" -Recurse -Force
Remove-Item "$($tempDir)main.zip" -Recurse -Force
Remove-Item $classicApps -Force -Recurse
```

## 15. CrapFixer (Builtbybel) — honorable mention

**Type:** Open-source WinForms app by Belim (Builtbybel) · **Source:** github.com/builtbybel/CrapFixer.

**How it works:** Tweaks are not hard-coded — they live in the text database `Wintweak2.ini` (each section = one tweak with `Path`, `ValueName`, `ValueType`, `RecommendedValue`, `DefaultValue`, optional `Path2…N` for multi-value tweaks; `<delete>`/`<deletevalue>` as default means *remove* on reset). The app first **analyzes** the system (shows which tweaks are not yet applied, i.e. the 'crap' it found), then **fixes** the selected ones; *Restore* writes `DefaultValue`. App removal uses `Winappx.ini` (a list of AppX name patterns) via `Remove-AppxPackage`. Extras: custom-tweak editor (add your own registry tweak), an online database updater, an *extensions* catalog of PowerShell scripts, and an optional **AI explain** feature that sends a tweak's definition to an AI model (your own API key) to explain what it does. Logs can be exported and viewed in a browser-based log analyzer.

## 16. Flyoobe (Builtbybel) — honorable mention

**Type:** Open-source WinForms app · **Source:** github.com/builtbybel/Flyoobe · formerly *Flyby11*. Two jobs: (1) **upgrade/install Windows 11 on unsupported hardware**, (2) an **OOBE/post-setup assistant** (debloat, privacy, personalization, app installs) you run right after installing Windows.

### 16.1 Windows 11 upgrade on unsupported hardware

You pick a Windows 11 ISO; Flyoobe mounts it (`Mount-DiskImage -ImagePath <iso>` via an encoded PowerShell command) and, in *Flyby mode*, starts `<iso>\sources\setupprep.exe /Product Server`. The Server setup path does not enforce the consumer Windows 11 hardware checks (TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, CPU list), but the normal client edition is installed as an in-place upgrade. Without Flyby mode it starts setup normally. The checks below are only used to report what your hardware fails. Configuration file `Upgrade.ini`:

```ini
; upgrade.ini - small, editable checks for the native Flyby11 mode
; Commands never live here. The actual setup launch stays in trusted code.

[Windows11]
MinimumRamGB=4
RecommendedFreeSpaceGB=25
MinimumMediaBuild=22000
Require64Bit=true
RequireTpm20=true
RequireSecureBoot=true
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1797):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Installs Windows 11 on unsupported hardware through the Server setup path; out of scope.

### 16.3 Setup actions (`Data/Actions/*/run.ps1`)

#### Chris Titus Tech's Windows Utility
Downloads and starts the current WinUtil script from its official project endpoint.

```powershell
# Options: Run utility

param([string]$choice)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
if ($choice -ne 'Run utility') { throw "Unknown option: $choice" }

$uri = 'https://christitus.com/win'
Write-Output "Downloading the current Chris Titus Tech WinUtil script from $uri ..."
$source = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($source)) { throw 'The WinUtil endpoint returned an empty script.' }

Write-Output 'Starting WinUtil...'
& ([scriptblock]::Create($source))
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1862):** Not suitable for PCOptimizer. Downloads and runs another tool; out of scope.

#### Clear the Windows icon cache
Rebuilds the current user's icon cache after setup. Explorer is restarted once.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
try {
    & ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache
    Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Remove-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\IconCache.db" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer" -Filter 'iconcache*' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Process explorer.exe
    exit 0
}
catch {
    Start-Process explorer.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Write-Error $_
    exit 1
}
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1863):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Same as U1355: an icon cache reset could be a quick fix on the Tools page.

#### Microsoft Defender maintenance
Update, repair or inspect Microsoft Defender using the original dynamic Flyoobe script.

```powershell
# Microsoft Defender maintenance (update signatures, repair, show status)
# Options: Update signatures; Repair definitions and update; Show Defender status

param([string]$choice)

function Get-MpCmdPath {
    $candidates = @(
        "$env:ProgramFiles\Windows Defender\MpCmdRun.exe",
        "$env:ProgramFiles\Microsoft Defender\MpCmdRun.exe"
    )
    foreach ($p in $candidates) { if (Test-Path $p) { return $p } }
    return $null
}

function Is-Admin {
    $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $pr = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal($id)
    return $pr.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Show-Status {
    try {
        $s = Get-MpComputerStatus
        Write-Output "=== Microsoft Defender Status ==="
        Write-Output ("Engine version:           {0}" -f $s.AMEngineVersion)
        Write-Output ("Platform version:         {0}" -f $s.AMProductVersion)
        Write-Output ("AV signature version:     {0}" -f $s.AntivirusSignatureVersion)
        Write-Output ("AV signature last update: {0}" -f $s.AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated)
        Write-Output ("AS signature version:     {0}" -f $s.AntispywareSignatureVersion)
        Write-Output ("Real-time protection:     {0}" -f $s.RealTimeProtectionEnabled)
        Write-Output ("NIS enabled:              {0}" -f $s.NISEnabled)
        Write-Output ("Service enabled:          {0}" -f $s.AMServiceEnabled)
    } catch {
        Write-Output "✘ Failed to read Defender status: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}

switch ($choice) {

    "Update signatures" {
        if (-not (Is-Admin)) {
            Write-Output "ℹ Tip: Run as Administrator for the most reliable results."
        }

        try {
            # Primary: PowerShell cmdlet
            Update-MpSignature -ErrorAction Stop
            Write-Output "✔ Signatures updated via Update-MpSignature."
        } catch {
            # Fallback: MpCmdRun
            $mp = Get-MpCmdPath
            if ($mp) {
                Write-Output "↻ Falling back to MpCmdRun.exe ..."
                & $mp -SignatureUpdate | Out-String | Write-Output
            } else {
                Write-Output "✘ MpCmdRun.exe not found and Update-MpSignature failed."
            }
```

#### Re-register built-in Windows apps
Re-registers the manifests of installed built-in apps for the current Windows installation. Useful when inbox apps no longer start.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$packages = @(Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers | Where-Object {
    $_.InstallLocation -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $_.InstallLocation 'AppxManifest.xml'))
})
if ($packages.Count -eq 0) { throw 'No installed app manifests were found.' }

$registered = 0
foreach ($package in $packages) {
    try {
        Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register (Join-Path $package.InstallLocation 'AppxManifest.xml') -ErrorAction Stop
        $registered++
    }
    catch {
        Write-Warning "$($package.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)"
    }
}
if ($registered -eq 0) { throw 'Windows could not re-register any built-in app.' }
Write-Output "Re-registered $registered of $($packages.Count) app packages."
```

> **PCOptimizer (U1869):** Could be added as a tool or page feature. Re-registering built-in apps (Add-AppxPackage -Register with the installed manifests, documented) could be a Health repair step for broken inbox apps.

#### Setup preflight
Checks for a pending restart, critically low disk space and other common setup problems before a recipe changes the PC.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# This action is deliberately read-only. Hard blockers fail the recipe;
# things that may be perfectly normal on some PCs are reported as warnings.
$blockers = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$warnings = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

function Write-CheckResult([string]$State, [string]$Message) {
    Write-Output ("[{0}] {1}" -f $State, $Message)
}

function Test-Administrator {
    $identity = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
    $principal = [Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]::new($identity)
    return $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
}

function Get-PendingRestartReasons {
    $reasons = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

    if (Test-Path 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\RebootPending') {
        $reasons.Add('Component Based Servicing')
    }
    if (Test-Path 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\RebootRequired') {
        $reasons.Add('Windows Update')
    }

    $sessionManager = Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager' -Name PendingFileRenameOperations -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $pendingFileOperations = @($sessionManager.PendingFileRenameOperations) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) }
    if ($pendingFileOperations.Count -gt 0) {
        $reasons.Add('pending file operations')
    }

    $activeName = (Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ActiveComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    $configuredName = (Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\ComputerName\ComputerName' -Name ComputerName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ComputerName
    if ($activeName -and $configuredName -and $activeName -ne $configuredName) {
        $reasons.Add('pending computer rename')
    }

    return $reasons
}

try {
    Write-Output '=== Flyoobe setup preflight ==='
    Write-Output 'This check does not change Windows.'

    if (Test-Administrator) {
        Write-CheckResult 'OK' 'Flyoobe is running as administrator.'
    }
    else {
        $blockers.Add('Flyoobe is not running as administrator.')
        Write-CheckResult 'BLOCKED' $blockers[$blockers.Count - 1]
    }

    $restartReasons = @(Get-PendingRestartReasons)
    if ($restartReasons.Count -eq 0) {
```

## Appendix: Already in PCOptimizer

Removed from the sections above because PCOptimizer already offers them. The note names the tweak id or the page.

### 1. Chris Titus Tech WinUtil

- **AppxDefault** (1.1 Tweak presets), U0004: Debloat page lists all of these except Calculator (protected on purpose) and StartExperiencesApp (part of Widgets; background.widgetsOff turns Widgets off by policy).
- **Activity History - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0005: privacy.activityHistoryOff (same three policy values).
- **Hibernation - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0006: power.hibernateOff.
- **Widgets - Remove** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0007: background.widgetsOff turns Widgets off with the documented policy; the WebExperience package stays protected because the shell uses it.
- **Location Tracking - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0010: privacy.locationOff (location consent store); map updates are in privacy.mapsTrafficOff.
- **ConsumerFeatures - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0012: privacy.consumerFeaturesOff.
- **Telemetry - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0013: privacy.telemetryOff plus the separate tweaks for advertising ID, tailored experiences, inking and typing, feedback notifications, app launch tracking and activity history.
- **Delivery Optimization - Disable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0014: network.deliveryOptimizationP2POff (same policy).
- **Restore Point - Create** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0016: Changes page: a restore point is created before the first change of each session.
- **End Task With Right Click - Enable** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0017: explorer.endTask.
- **Prevent Device Companion Apps** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0019: privacy.deviceMetadataOff.
- **Disk Cleanup - Run** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0020: Cleanup page (temporary files, update downloads, error reports, Delivery Optimization cache, superseded components without /ResetBase).
- **Temporary Files - Remove** (1.2 Essential Tweaks), U0021: Cleanup page (Windows and user temp folders).
- **Microsoft OneDrive - Remove** (1.3 Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION), U0028: Debloat page: Uninstall OneDrive.
- **Visual Effects - Set to Best Performance** (1.3 Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION), U0030: visual.bestPerformance. Not taken over: menu show delay and keyboard delay (preferences) and taskbar buttons (Personalize items below).
- **Storage Sense - Disable** (1.3 Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION), U0032: storage.storageSenseOn (the same value, turned on instead of off; undo turns it off).
- **Right-Click Menu Previous Layout - Enable** (1.3 Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION), U0038: explorer.classicContextMenu.
- **IPv6 - Set IPv4 as Preferred** (1.3 Advanced Tweaks - CAUTION), U0039: network.preferIpv4 (same DisabledComponents bit).
